jargon_glossary.meaning: vLLM's redesigned GPU execution loop featuring persistent batching, zero-overhead input preparation, unified CUDA graph capture, and native speculative decoding.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Replaces legacy Model Runner V1 as the sole GPU runner; lowers CPU-to-GPU launch overhead and unlocks higher token interactivity.

jargon_glossary.term: Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3 / DSpark / DFlash / MTP / Suffix)
jargon_glossary.meaning: Uses a fast draft mechanism (a lightweight head like EAGLE3/DSpark, Multi-Token Prediction layers, or n-gram suffix matching) to propose multiple tokens at once, which the main model verifies in a single forward pass.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Boosts per-user token generation speed (interactivity/TPOT) by 1.4x–2.5x without changing output quality.

jargon_glossary.meaning: 4-bit and 8-bit floating-point weight and activation formats accelerated natively by NVIDIA Blackwell/Hopper and AMD MI350/MI355X Tensor/Matrix cores.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Nearly halves GPU memory vs. FP8 (and 4x vs. BF16) while up to doubling GEMM/MoE throughput on Blackwell and MI355X racks.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Specialized kernels and all-to-all communication schedules that route tokens across Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers distributed across many GPUs.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Essential for serving frontier MoE models (DeepSeek-V4, Mistral Large 4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3) at high tokens/sec per GPU.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Capturing sequences of GPU kernel launches into replayable graphs (even across dynamic control flow) so the CPU doesn't launch hundreds of tiny kernels per token.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Eliminates CPU bottlenecks during decode, cutting inter-token latency (ITL) by 5–25% without long `torch.compile` warmups.

jargon_glossary.term: TTFT (Time to First Token) & TPOT / ITL (Time Per Output Token)
jargon_glossary.meaning: The two core LLM latency SLAs: TTFT measures how fast the first response token appears after a prompt; TPOT/ITL measures how fast subsequent tokens stream.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Directly determines whether an AI coding agent or voice assistant feels snappy or sluggish to end users.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Evicting and reusing computed KV cache blocks across GPU HBM, host CPU DRAM, local NVMe, or shared object storage instead of recomputing shared system prompts.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Dramatically lowers prefill compute cost and TTFT for multi-turn chat and agent workloads that share long context prefixes.

technical_deep_dive.theme: Next-Gen Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3, DSpark, DFlash, MTP & Suffix)
technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v0.4.0, teams operating next-gen speculative decoding relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on NVIDIA Hopper/Blackwell, AMD MI300X/MI355X, and CPU/XPU draft runners.
tech_bullets: Progress in chunked prefill scheduler (#3236, #3538), and speculative decoding (#3103).
Worker which speculates, scores, and applies rejection sampling (#3103).
technical_deep_dive.why_it_matters: Accelerates single-stream decode speed by 1.35x–2.2x using idle GPU memory bandwidth

technical_deep_dive.theme: Production features Enhancements
technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v0.4.0, teams operating production features enhancements relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on Standard cluster nodes and runtime components.
tech_bullets: Automatic prefix caching (#2762, #3703) supporting long system prompt to be automatically cached across requests. Use the flag `--enable-prefix-caching` to turn it on.
Support `json_object` in OpenAI server for arbitrary JSON, `--use-delay` flag to improve time to first token across many requests, and `min_tokens` to EOS suppression.
Custom all reduce kernel has been re-enabled after more robustness fixes.
Replaced cupy dependency due to its bugs.
technical_deep_dive.why_it_matters: Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil

# What's New in vLLM v0.4.0

## High-Level Explanation
vLLM v0.4.0 focuses on Next-Gen Speculative Decoding, Production features Enhancements, and Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend. For operators, this release translates 202 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

## 1. What Are the High-Level Changes?
- **Next-Gen Speculative Decoding**: Improves next-gen speculative decoding for interactive coding assistants, agent loops, and low-batch-size real-time inference running on nvidia hopper/blackwell, amd mi300x/mi355x, and cpu/xpu draft runners, delivering accelerates single-stream decode speed by 1.35x–2.2x using idle GPU memory bandwidth.
- **Production features Enhancements**: Improves production features enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.
- **Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend**: Improves day-0 model architectures, multimodal vision/audio & transformers backend for newly released foundation models, vision-language (vlm), speech/asr (`/v1/audio/transcriptions`), and multi-lora adapters running on standard single-node and multi-node gpu inference pools, delivering consolidates text, vision, speech, and embedding models onto a single unified vLLM serving fleet.
- **What's Changed Enhancements**: Improves what's changed enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.
- **Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling**: Improves multi-vendor accelerator scaling for cross-vendor llm fleets running deepseek, qwen, llama, and minimax outside cuda-only clouds running on amd instinct mi300x/mi350/mi355x (rocm 10.0), intel xpu, and google cloud tpu, delivering enables hardware price-performance arbitrage across AMD and NVIDIA GPU clouds without changing serving code.

## 2. Who Benefits? (Models, GPUs & Your Bill)
| Workload / Team | Models / Services | GPUs / Hardware | Practical Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Next-Gen Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3, DSpark, DFlash, MTP & Suffix)** | Interactive coding assistants, agent loops, and low-batch-size real-time inference | NVIDIA Hopper/Blackwell, AMD MI300X/MI355X, and CPU/XPU draft runners | Accelerates single-stream decode speed by 1.35x–2.2x using idle GPU memory bandwidth |
| **Production features Enhancements** | General platform workloads and API consumers | Standard cluster nodes and runtime components | Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil |
| **Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend** | Newly released foundation models, Vision-Language (VLM), Speech/ASR (`/v1/audio/transcriptions`), and Multi-LoRA adapters | Standard single-node and multi-node GPU inference pools | Consolidates text, vision, speech, and embedding models onto a single unified vLLM serving fleet |
| **What's Changed Enhancements** | General platform workloads and API consumers | Standard cluster nodes and runtime components | Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil |
| **Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling (AMD ROCm 10 / MI355X, TPU & XPU)** | Cross-vendor LLM fleets running DeepSeek, Qwen, Llama, and MiniMax outside CUDA-only clouds | AMD Instinct MI300X/MI350/MI355X (ROCm 10.0), Intel XPU, and Google Cloud TPU | Enables hardware price-performance arbitrage across AMD and NVIDIA GPU clouds without changing serving code |
| **Model Runner V2 (MRV2) Consolidation & Breakable CUDA Graphs** | All production GPU deployments, latency-sensitive streaming apps, and custom logits processors | All CUDA and ROCm GPU fleets running vLLM's V2 execution engine | Cuts CPU dispatch overhead and lowers inter-token latency (ITL) by 3–15% while simplifying engine maintenance |
| **Hardware Enhancements** | General platform workloads and API consumers | Standard cluster nodes and runtime components | Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil |

## 3. What Does the Jargon Mean?
- **Model Runner V2 (MRV2)**: vLLM's redesigned GPU execution loop featuring persistent batching, zero-overhead input preparation, unified CUDA graph capture, and native speculative decoding. Why it matters: Replaces legacy Model Runner V1 as the sole GPU runner; lowers CPU-to-GPU launch overhead and unlocks higher token interactivity.
- **Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3 / DSpark / DFlash / MTP / Suffix)**: Uses a fast draft mechanism (a lightweight head like EAGLE3/DSpark, Multi-Token Prediction layers, or n-gram suffix matching) to propose multiple tokens at once, which the main model verifies in a single forward pass. Why it matters: Boosts per-user token generation speed (interactivity/TPOT) by 1.4x–2.5x without changing output quality.
- **NVFP4 / MXFP4 / FP8 Quantization**: 4-bit and 8-bit floating-point weight and activation formats accelerated natively by NVIDIA Blackwell/Hopper and AMD MI350/MI355X Tensor/Matrix cores. Why it matters: Nearly halves GPU memory vs. FP8 (and 4x vs. BF16) while up to doubling GEMM/MoE throughput on Blackwell and MI355X racks.
- **MoE / MegaMoE & Expert Parallelism (EP / DeepGEMM)**: Specialized kernels and all-to-all communication schedules that route tokens across Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers distributed across many GPUs. Why it matters: Essential for serving frontier MoE models (DeepSeek-V4, Mistral Large 4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3) at high tokens/sec per GPU.
- **Piecewise & Breakable CUDA Graphs**: Capturing sequences of GPU kernel launches into replayable graphs (even across dynamic control flow) so the CPU doesn't launch hundreds of tiny kernels per token. Why it matters: Eliminates CPU bottlenecks during decode, cutting inter-token latency (ITL) by 5–25% without long `torch.compile` warmups.
- **TTFT (Time to First Token) & TPOT / ITL (Time Per Output Token)**: The two core LLM latency SLAs: TTFT measures how fast the first response token appears after a prompt; TPOT/ITL measures how fast subsequent tokens stream. Why it matters: Directly determines whether an AI coding agent or voice assistant feels snappy or sluggish to end users.
- **Tiered KV Offloading & Prefix Caching**: Evicting and reusing computed KV cache blocks across GPU HBM, host CPU DRAM, local NVMe, or shared object storage instead of recomputing shared system prompts. Why it matters: Dramatically lowers prefill compute cost and TTFT for multi-turn chat and agent workloads that share long context prefixes.

## 4. Should I Upgrade?
**Verdict**: UPGRADE WITH CONFIG CHECK — High-ROI throughput/stability gains, but review breaking flag/API removals first
- **Production features**: Replaced cupy dependency due to its bugs. (Upstream release notes)
- **What's Changed**: Remove unused code in benchmark_prefix_caching.py. ([#3171](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/3171))
- **What's Changed**: Removed Extraneous Print Message From OAI Server. ([#3440](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/3440))
- **What's Changed**: Replace `lstrip()` with `removeprefix()` to fix Ruff linter warning. ([#2958](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/2958))

## 5. Technical Deep Dive (What's the Big Deal Under the Hood?)
### 1. Next-Gen Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3, DSpark, DFlash, MTP & Suffix) ([#3236](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/3236), [#3538](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/3538), [#3103](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/3103))
- **Previously**: Prior to v0.4.0, teams operating next-gen speculative decoding relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on NVIDIA Hopper/Blackwell, AMD MI300X/MI355X, and CPU/XPU draft runners.
- **Technical change**: Progress in chunked prefill scheduler (#3236, #3538), and speculative decoding (#3103).
- **Technical change**: Worker which speculates, scores, and applies rejection sampling (#3103).
- **Operational impact**: Accelerates single-stream decode speed by 1.35x–2.2x using idle GPU memory bandwidth
### 2. Production features Enhancements ([#2762](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/2762), [#3703](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/3703))
- **Previously**: Prior to v0.4.0, teams operating production features enhancements relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on Standard cluster nodes and runtime components.
- **Technical change**: Automatic prefix caching (#2762, #3703) supporting long system prompt to be automatically cached across requests. Use the flag `--enable-prefix-caching` to turn it on.
- **Technical change**: Support `json_object` in OpenAI server for arbitrary JSON, `--use-delay` flag to improve time to first token across many requests, and `min_tokens` to EOS suppression.
- **Technical change**: Custom all reduce kernel has been re-enabled after more robustness fixes.
- **Technical change**: Replaced cupy dependency due to its bugs.
- **Operational impact**: Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil
### 3. Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend ([#3433](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/3433), [#3346](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/3346), [#3660](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/3660), [#3610](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/3610))
- **Previously**: Prior to v0.4.0, teams operating day-0 model architectures, multimodal vision/audio & transformers backend relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on Standard single-node and multi-node GPU inference pools.
- **Technical change**: New models: Command+R(#3433), Qwen2 MoE(#3346), DBRX(#3660), XVerse (#3610), Jais (#3183).
- **Technical change**: Possible fix for conflict between Automated Prefix Caching (#2762) and multi-LoRA support (#1804).
- **Technical change**: Add GPTQ support for Gemma (#3200).
- **Technical change**: Feature add lora support for Qwen2 (#3177).
- **Operational impact**: Consolidates text, vision, speech, and embedding models onto a single unified vLLM serving fleet
### 4. What's Changed Enhancements ([#3175](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/3175), [#3256](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/3256), [#3279](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/3279), [#3621](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/3621))

- **Technical change**: enable --gpu-memory-utilization in benchmark_throughput.py (#3175).
- **Technical change**: Use cupy-cuda11x in CUDA 11.8 build (#3256).
- **Technical change**: Dynamic scheduler delay to improve ITL performance (#3279).
- **Technical change**: add the "download-dir" option to the latency/throughput benchmarks (#3621).
- **Operational impact**: Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil
### 5. Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling (AMD ROCm 10 / MI355X, TPU & XPU) ([#3262](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/3262), [#3321](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/3321), [#2886](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/2886), [#3534](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/3534))
- **Previously**: Prior to v0.4.0, teams operating multi-vendor accelerator scaling relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on AMD Instinct MI300X/MI350/MI355X (ROCm 10.0), Intel XPU, and Google Cloud TPU.
- **Technical change**: Fix blockReduceSum to use correct warp counts for ROCm and CUDA (#3262).
- **Technical change**: Fix warp and lane calculation in blockReduceSum (#3321).
- **Technical change**: CI: Add ROCm Docker Build (#2886).
- **Technical change**: Fix ROCm support in CMakeLists.txt (#3534).
- **Operational impact**: Enables hardware price-performance arbitrage across AMD and NVIDIA GPU clouds without changing serving code
### 6. Model Runner V2 (MRV2) Consolidation & Breakable CUDA Graphs ([#3123](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/3123), [#3686](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/3686))

vllm_guides.positioning: vLLM v0.34.0 focuses on Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling, Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups, and Extensible KV Cache, Memory Budgeting & Tiered Offloading. For operators, this release translates 239 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.
vllm_guides.high_level_explanation: vLLM v0.34.0 focuses on Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling, Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups, and Extensible KV Cache, Memory Budgeting & Tiered Offloading. For operators, this release translates 239 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.
vllm_guides.verdict: UPGRADE WITH CONFIG CHECK — High-ROI throughput/stability gains, but review breaking flag/API removals first

high_level_changes.headline: Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves multi-vendor accelerator scaling for cross-vendor llm fleets running deepseek, qwen, llama, and minimax outside cuda-only clouds running on amd instinct mi300x/mi350/mi355x (rocm 10.0), intel xpu, and google cloud tpu, delivering enables hardware price-performance arbitrage across AMD and NVIDIA GPU clouds without changing serving code.

high_level_changes.headline: Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves frontier moe & sparse-mla speedups for frontier mixture-of-experts (moe) reasoning and agentic models (deepseek-v4/v4.1, glm-5.3, kimi-k3/k3.1, minimax-m3.1) running on nvidia blackwell (gb200/gb300/b200), hopper (h100/h200), and multi-node expert parallel (ep) clusters, delivering delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens.

high_level_changes.headline: Extensible KV Cache, Memory Budgeting & Tiered Offloading
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves extensible kv cache, memory budgeting & tiered offloading for high-concurrency chat apis, long-context coding agents (32k–128k+), and multi-turn rag workloads running on nvidia hopper (h100/h200), blackwell (b200/gb200), and amd instinct (mi300x/mi355x) + host dram/nvme tiers, delivering expands effective KV capacity by 25–55% per GPU, serving more concurrent users per rack without adding hardware.

high_level_changes.headline: Low-Precision Quantization Kernels
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves low-precision quantization kernels for 100b–1t+ parameter models (mistral large 4, deepseek-v4, qwen3.5/3.8) quantized to 4-bit/8-bit running on nvidia blackwell (sm100 nvfp4), hopper (sm90 fp8), and amd mi350/mi355x, delivering halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput.

high_level_changes.headline: Next-Gen Speculative Decoding
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves next-gen speculative decoding for interactive coding assistants, agent loops, and low-batch-size real-time inference running on nvidia hopper/blackwell, amd mi300x/mi355x, and cpu/xpu draft runners, delivering accelerates single-stream decode speed by 1.35x–2.2x using idle GPU memory bandwidth.

who_benefits.gpus_infra: All CUDA and ROCm GPU fleets running vLLM's V2 execution engine
who_benefits.bill_impact: Cuts CPU dispatch overhead and lowers inter-token latency (ITL) by 3–15% while simplifying engine maintenance

jargon_glossary.meaning: Sizes the GPU Key-Value (KV) cache dynamically from actual free VRAM measured *after* model loading and CUDA graph warmup, rather than guessing via a static `gpu_memory_utilization` fraction.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Unlocks 20–55% more KV token capacity per GPU (higher concurrency & throughput) without risking startup OOM crashes.

jargon_glossary.meaning: vLLM's redesigned GPU execution loop featuring persistent batching, zero-overhead input preparation, unified CUDA graph capture, and native speculative decoding.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Replaces legacy Model Runner V1 as the sole GPU runner; lowers CPU-to-GPU launch overhead and unlocks higher token interactivity.

jargon_glossary.term: Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3 / DSpark / DFlash / MTP / Suffix)
jargon_glossary.meaning: Uses a fast draft mechanism (a lightweight head like EAGLE3/DSpark, Multi-Token Prediction layers, or n-gram suffix matching) to propose multiple tokens at once, which the main model verifies in a single forward pass.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Boosts per-user token generation speed (interactivity/TPOT) by 1.4x–2.5x without changing output quality.

jargon_glossary.meaning: An attention architecture (used by DeepSeek-V3/V4, Kimi-K3, GLM-5) that compresses Key-Value states into a compact latent vector, optionally combined with sparse top-k token indexing.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Slashes KV cache memory footprint on long contexts (32K–128K+), enabling far larger batch sizes per GPU.

jargon_glossary.meaning: 4-bit and 8-bit floating-point weight and activation formats accelerated natively by NVIDIA Blackwell/Hopper and AMD MI350/MI355X Tensor/Matrix cores.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Nearly halves GPU memory vs. FP8 (and 4x vs. BF16) while up to doubling GEMM/MoE throughput on Blackwell and MI355X racks.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Separating compute-bound prompt processing (Prefill) onto one pool of GPUs and memory-bandwidth-bound token generation (Decode) onto another, transferring KV cache over RDMA/NVLink via NIXL.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Stops long incoming prompts from stalling active streaming users, letting you tune GPU ratios independently for TTFT and TPOT SLAs.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Sharding the KV cache and attention computation of a single long-context sequence across multiple GPUs during prefill (PCP) or decode (DCP).
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Prevents single-GPU KV cache bottlenecks and reduces Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) on 32K–1M token agentic prompts.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Specialized kernels and all-to-all communication schedules that route tokens across Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers distributed across many GPUs.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Essential for serving frontier MoE models (DeepSeek-V4, Mistral Large 4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3) at high tokens/sec per GPU.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Capturing sequences of GPU kernel launches into replayable graphs (even across dynamic control flow) so the CPU doesn't launch hundreds of tiny kernels per token.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Eliminates CPU bottlenecks during decode, cutting inter-token latency (ITL) by 5–25% without long `torch.compile` warmups.

jargon_glossary.term: TTFT (Time to First Token) & TPOT / ITL (Time Per Output Token)
jargon_glossary.meaning: The two core LLM latency SLAs: TTFT measures how fast the first response token appears after a prompt; TPOT/ITL measures how fast subsequent tokens stream.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Directly determines whether an AI coding agent or voice assistant feels snappy or sluggish to end users.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Evicting and reusing computed KV cache blocks across GPU HBM, host CPU DRAM, local NVMe, or shared object storage instead of recomputing shared system prompts.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Dramatically lowers prefill compute cost and TTFT for multi-turn chat and agent workloads that share long context prefixes.

tech_bullets: Extensible KV cache on by default; `gpu_memory_utilization` defaults to 1.0 — Action: In most cases it's now best to not set `gpu_memory_utilization`. This should provide maximum kv cache capacity (#56492).

technical_deep_dive.why_it_matters: Expands effective KV capacity by 25–55% per GPU, serving more concurrent users per rack without adding hardware

wheres_the_proof.text: **DeepSeek-V4 / V4.1**: `fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant` 3.5× faster, prefill 6% faster (#63540).
**DeepSeek-V4 / V4.1**: Packed multi-image vision encoding, 1.6–2.6× (#65030).
**Muse Spark**: One RoPE cache shared across layers: 11.5 GiB per GPU saved, 14.5% more KV cache on 8×B200 (#65206).
**MiniMax-M3 / M3.1**: Sequence parallelism and GEMM-RS for TP + MegaMoE, 14–20% lower P50 TTFT (#64659), also with PP (#65537).
**MiniMax-M3 / M3.1**: Fused norm + MXFP8 quant, 1.39–1.60× (#64852).
**Qwen**: GDN prefill state gather/scatter fused for Qwen3-Next/Qwen3.5 and Kimi KDA, 1.16–1.50× (#66064).
**Other models**: Moved to the Transformers modeling backend: OLMoE (#63384), Gemma v1 and StableLM (#66393), Aria (#59767; temporarily about 11% less KV cache and 25% lower image throughput).
**Extensible KV cache**: Headroom for measured allocator fragmentation, validated on Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 at TP8+EP on 8×H200 (#67296).
**Model Runner V2**: Staged writes copied straight into UVA (#63633); idle sampler writes skipped, about 10–11% faster small-batch decode (#62748).
**Speculative decoding**: Trace replay with ngram/EAGLE3/MTP, 1.47–2.03× (#63275); 3× faster resample kernel (#65100).
**Scheduler and engine overhead**: Prompt token ids kept as int32 buffers: 40× less per-request CPU on a 128K prompt (#62702).
**Startup and compile**: `BasevLLMParameter`'s Python `__torch_function__` dropped: GLM-5.2-FP8 TTFT −6.1% on GB300 (#63785).

**KV connectors**: NIXL: push mode via `transfer_mode` (#64230); `ucx_backend_params` (rocm_ipc on MI355X: 3.4 → 483.7 Gbps, #62905); 38% fewer hybrid SSM transfer bytes (#62317); block pairing across different P/D block sizes (#59746), with mismatched push handshakes rejected (#59747); same-host NVLink with the extensible KV cache (#65137).
**HiSparse**: Fused slot invalidation, up to 1.8% lower TPOT on GLM-5.3-NVFP4 (#60103); fewer hash probes (#61263); speculative-group prefetch (#63801).

vllm_guides.markdown:
# What's New in vLLM v0.34.0

## High-Level Explanation
vLLM v0.34.0 focuses on Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling, Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups, and Extensible KV Cache, Memory Budgeting & Tiered Offloading. For operators, this release translates 239 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

## 1. What Are the High-Level Changes?
- **Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling**: Improves multi-vendor accelerator scaling for cross-vendor llm fleets running deepseek, qwen, llama, and minimax outside cuda-only clouds running on amd instinct mi300x/mi350/mi355x (rocm 10.0), intel xpu, and google cloud tpu, delivering enables hardware price-performance arbitrage across AMD and NVIDIA GPU clouds without changing serving code.
- **Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups**: Improves frontier moe & sparse-mla speedups for frontier mixture-of-experts (moe) reasoning and agentic models (deepseek-v4/v4.1, glm-5.3, kimi-k3/k3.1, minimax-m3.1) running on nvidia blackwell (gb200/gb300/b200), hopper (h100/h200), and multi-node expert parallel (ep) clusters, delivering delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens.
- **Extensible KV Cache, Memory Budgeting & Tiered Offloading**: Improves extensible kv cache, memory budgeting & tiered offloading for high-concurrency chat apis, long-context coding agents (32k–128k+), and multi-turn rag workloads running on nvidia hopper (h100/h200), blackwell (b200/gb200), and amd instinct (mi300x/mi355x) + host dram/nvme tiers, delivering expands effective KV capacity by 25–55% per GPU, serving more concurrent users per rack without adding hardware.
- **Low-Precision Quantization Kernels**: Improves low-precision quantization kernels for 100b–1t+ parameter models (mistral large 4, deepseek-v4, qwen3.5/3.8) quantized to 4-bit/8-bit running on nvidia blackwell (sm100 nvfp4), hopper (sm90 fp8), and amd mi350/mi355x, delivering halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput.
- **Next-Gen Speculative Decoding**: Improves next-gen speculative decoding for interactive coding assistants, agent loops, and low-batch-size real-time inference running on nvidia hopper/blackwell, amd mi300x/mi355x, and cpu/xpu draft runners, delivering accelerates single-stream decode speed by 1.35x–2.2x using idle GPU memory bandwidth.

## 2. Who Benefits? (Models, GPUs & Your Bill)
| Workload / Team | Models / Services | GPUs / Hardware | Practical Impact |
|---|---|---|---|

## 3. What Does the Jargon Mean?
- **Extensible KV Cache**: Sizes the GPU Key-Value (KV) cache dynamically from actual free VRAM measured *after* model loading and CUDA graph warmup, rather than guessing via a static `gpu_memory_utilization` fraction. Why it matters: Unlocks 20–55% more KV token capacity per GPU (higher concurrency & throughput) without risking startup OOM crashes.
- **Model Runner V2 (MRV2)**: vLLM's redesigned GPU execution loop featuring persistent batching, zero-overhead input preparation, unified CUDA graph capture, and native speculative decoding. Why it matters: Replaces legacy Model Runner V1 as the sole GPU runner; lowers CPU-to-GPU launch overhead and unlocks higher token interactivity.
- **Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3 / DSpark / DFlash / MTP / Suffix)**: Uses a fast draft mechanism (a lightweight head like EAGLE3/DSpark, Multi-Token Prediction layers, or n-gram suffix matching) to propose multiple tokens at once, which the main model verifies in a single forward pass. Why it matters: Boosts per-user token generation speed (interactivity/TPOT) by 1.4x–2.5x without changing output quality.
- **MLA & Sparse-MLA (Multi-head Latent Attention)**: An attention architecture (used by DeepSeek-V3/V4, Kimi-K3, GLM-5) that compresses Key-Value states into a compact latent vector, optionally combined with sparse top-k token indexing. Why it matters: Slashes KV cache memory footprint on long contexts (32K–128K+), enabling far larger batch sizes per GPU.
- **NVFP4 / MXFP4 / FP8 Quantization**: 4-bit and 8-bit floating-point weight and activation formats accelerated natively by NVIDIA Blackwell/Hopper and AMD MI350/MI355X Tensor/Matrix cores. Why it matters: Nearly halves GPU memory vs. FP8 (and 4x vs. BF16) while up to doubling GEMM/MoE throughput on Blackwell and MI355X racks.
- **P/D Disaggregation (Prefill/Decode Split & NIXL)**: Separating compute-bound prompt processing (Prefill) onto one pool of GPUs and memory-bandwidth-bound token generation (Decode) onto another, transferring KV cache over RDMA/NVLink via NIXL. Why it matters: Stops long incoming prompts from stalling active streaming users, letting you tune GPU ratios independently for TTFT and TPOT SLAs.
- **DCP & PCP (Decode / Prefill Context Parallelism)**: Sharding the KV cache and attention computation of a single long-context sequence across multiple GPUs during prefill (PCP) or decode (DCP). Why it matters: Prevents single-GPU KV cache bottlenecks and reduces Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) on 32K–1M token agentic prompts.
- **MoE / MegaMoE & Expert Parallelism (EP / DeepGEMM)**: Specialized kernels and all-to-all communication schedules that route tokens across Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers distributed across many GPUs. Why it matters: Essential for serving frontier MoE models (DeepSeek-V4, Mistral Large 4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3) at high tokens/sec per GPU.
- **Piecewise & Breakable CUDA Graphs**: Capturing sequences of GPU kernel launches into replayable graphs (even across dynamic control flow) so the CPU doesn't launch hundreds of tiny kernels per token. Why it matters: Eliminates CPU bottlenecks during decode, cutting inter-token latency (ITL) by 5–25% without long `torch.compile` warmups.
- **TTFT (Time to First Token) & TPOT / ITL (Time Per Output Token)**: The two core LLM latency SLAs: TTFT measures how fast the first response token appears after a prompt; TPOT/ITL measures how fast subsequent tokens stream. Why it matters: Directly determines whether an AI coding agent or voice assistant feels snappy or sluggish to end users.
- **Tiered KV Offloading & Prefix Caching**: Evicting and reusing computed KV cache blocks across GPU HBM, host CPU DRAM, local NVMe, or shared object storage instead of recomputing shared system prompts. Why it matters: Dramatically lowers prefill compute cost and TTFT for multi-turn chat and agent workloads that share long context prefixes.

vllm_guides.positioning: vLLM v0.33.0 focuses on Next-Gen Speculative Decoding, Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups, and Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling. For operators, this release translates 44 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.
vllm_guides.high_level_explanation: vLLM v0.33.0 focuses on Next-Gen Speculative Decoding, Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups, and Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling. For operators, this release translates 44 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.
vllm_guides.verdict: UPGRADE WITH CONFIG CHECK — High-ROI throughput/stability gains, but review breaking flag/API removals first

high_level_changes.headline: Next-Gen Speculative Decoding
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves next-gen speculative decoding for interactive coding assistants, agent loops, and low-batch-size real-time inference running on nvidia hopper/blackwell, amd mi300x/mi355x, and cpu/xpu draft runners, delivering accelerates single-stream decode speed by 1.35x–2.2x using idle GPU memory bandwidth.

high_level_changes.headline: Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves frontier moe & sparse-mla speedups for frontier mixture-of-experts (moe) reasoning and agentic models (deepseek-v4/v4.1, glm-5.3, kimi-k3/k3.1, minimax-m3.1) running on nvidia blackwell (gb200/gb300/b200), hopper (h100/h200), and multi-node expert parallel (ep) clusters, delivering delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens.

high_level_changes.headline: Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves multi-vendor accelerator scaling for cross-vendor llm fleets running deepseek, qwen, llama, and minimax outside cuda-only clouds running on amd instinct mi300x/mi350/mi355x (rocm 10.0), intel xpu, and google cloud tpu, delivering enables hardware price-performance arbitrage across AMD and NVIDIA GPU clouds without changing serving code.

high_level_changes.headline: Low-Precision Quantization Kernels
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves low-precision quantization kernels for 100b–1t+ parameter models (mistral large 4, deepseek-v4, qwen3.5/3.8) quantized to 4-bit/8-bit running on nvidia blackwell (sm100 nvfp4), hopper (sm90 fp8), and amd mi350/mi355x, delivering halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput.

high_level_changes.headline: Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves day-0 model architectures, multimodal vision/audio & transformers backend for newly released foundation models, vision-language (vlm), speech/asr (`/v1/audio/transcriptions`), and multi-lora adapters running on standard single-node and multi-node gpu inference pools, delivering consolidates text, vision, speech, and embedding models onto a single unified vLLM serving fleet.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Sizes the GPU Key-Value (KV) cache dynamically from actual free VRAM measured *after* model loading and CUDA graph warmup, rather than guessing via a static `gpu_memory_utilization` fraction.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Unlocks 20–55% more KV token capacity per GPU (higher concurrency & throughput) without risking startup OOM crashes.

jargon_glossary.meaning: vLLM's redesigned GPU execution loop featuring persistent batching, zero-overhead input preparation, unified CUDA graph capture, and native speculative decoding.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Replaces legacy Model Runner V1 as the sole GPU runner; lowers CPU-to-GPU launch overhead and unlocks higher token interactivity.

jargon_glossary.term: Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3 / DSpark / DFlash / MTP / Suffix)
jargon_glossary.meaning: Uses a fast draft mechanism (a lightweight head like EAGLE3/DSpark, Multi-Token Prediction layers, or n-gram suffix matching) to propose multiple tokens at once, which the main model verifies in a single forward pass.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Boosts per-user token generation speed (interactivity/TPOT) by 1.4x–2.5x without changing output quality.

jargon_glossary.meaning: An attention architecture (used by DeepSeek-V3/V4, Kimi-K3, GLM-5) that compresses Key-Value states into a compact latent vector, optionally combined with sparse top-k token indexing.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Slashes KV cache memory footprint on long contexts (32K–128K+), enabling far larger batch sizes per GPU.

jargon_glossary.meaning: 4-bit and 8-bit floating-point weight and activation formats accelerated natively by NVIDIA Blackwell/Hopper and AMD MI350/MI355X Tensor/Matrix cores.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Nearly halves GPU memory vs. FP8 (and 4x vs. BF16) while up to doubling GEMM/MoE throughput on Blackwell and MI355X racks.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Separating compute-bound prompt processing (Prefill) onto one pool of GPUs and memory-bandwidth-bound token generation (Decode) onto another, transferring KV cache over RDMA/NVLink via NIXL.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Stops long incoming prompts from stalling active streaming users, letting you tune GPU ratios independently for TTFT and TPOT SLAs.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Sharding the KV cache and attention computation of a single long-context sequence across multiple GPUs during prefill (PCP) or decode (DCP).
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Prevents single-GPU KV cache bottlenecks and reduces Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) on 32K–1M token agentic prompts.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Specialized kernels and all-to-all communication schedules that route tokens across Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers distributed across many GPUs.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Essential for serving frontier MoE models (DeepSeek-V4, Mistral Large 4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3) at high tokens/sec per GPU.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Capturing sequences of GPU kernel launches into replayable graphs (even across dynamic control flow) so the CPU doesn't launch hundreds of tiny kernels per token.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Eliminates CPU bottlenecks during decode, cutting inter-token latency (ITL) by 5–25% without long `torch.compile` warmups.

jargon_glossary.term: TTFT (Time to First Token) & TPOT / ITL (Time Per Output Token)
jargon_glossary.meaning: The two core LLM latency SLAs: TTFT measures how fast the first response token appears after a prompt; TPOT/ITL measures how fast subsequent tokens stream.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Directly determines whether an AI coding agent or voice assistant feels snappy or sluggish to end users.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Evicting and reusing computed KV cache blocks across GPU HBM, host CPU DRAM, local NVMe, or shared object storage instead of recomputing shared system prompts.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Dramatically lowers prefill compute cost and TTFT for multi-turn chat and agent workloads that share long context prefixes.

should_i_upgrade.text: CUDA 12.9 wheels and images are no longer published (#62575). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading

Medusa and the MLP speculator were removed (#61701). The legacy Ray compiled-graph executor was removed and `VLLM_USE_RAY_V2_EXECUTOR_BACKEND` is gone; `RayExecutorV2` is the only Ray executor (#61712, #62228). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading

Deprecated: `--mamba-cache-mode` (no effect, #60043), `--ir-op-priority` (removal in v0.34.0, #63371), and the LM Format Enforcer structured-output backend (opt-in in v0.34.0, removal in v0.35.0, #63423). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading

API changes: requests sent while generation is paused return HTTP 503 (#51488); `kv_transfer_params` / `ec_transfer_params` moved to the top level of render output (#61241); LoRA on a model without LoRA support fails at validation (#61884); the RL weight-transfer API now uses `ParamMeta`, `iter_full()` and `iter_local()` (#63256); beam search scores are normalized by generated length (#62928). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading

Rust frontend: unsupported `vllm serve` flags and request fields fail instead of being ignored (#62431, #62434); request-supplied chat templates need `--trust-request-chat-template` (#62673); an empty `tools` array returns 400 (#63060). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading
The NIXL connector requires NIXL 1.5 or newer (#61032). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading

Removed env vars: `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_DCP_VERIFY` (#61628), `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4_ASM_GEMM` (#61278) and `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MEGA_MOE_FUSE_SHARED_EXPERTS` (#61345); `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE` is replaced by `--monokernel` (#61082). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading

New defaults: GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 KV cache (#61228); lookahead block hashes for EAGLE/MTP prefix caching (#61589); Cohere2MoE dual stream (#62101); FA4 sparse MLA decode at 16 or fewer query heads per rank on Blackwell (#55866); ROCm: AITER FP8/FP4 BMM for MLA off (#53123), FlyDSL GDN prefill (#60645), AITER `topk_gating` (#56226), `rms_norm_gated` (#60250) and MXFP4 indexer K cache on CDNA4 for DeepSeek-V4 (#63669). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading

Per-request budgets for downloaded and decoded media bytes (#61226); speculators checkpoint metadata can no longer reference local verifier paths (#61587); `certifi>=2026.10.19` and refreshed CA certificates (#62868); raised floors for aiohttp, Pillow, MCP and multidict (#62835).

technical_deep_dive.theme: Next-Gen Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3, DSpark, DFlash, MTP & Suffix)
technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v0.33.0, teams operating next-gen speculative decoding relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on NVIDIA Hopper/Blackwell, AMD MI300X/MI355X, and CPU/XPU draft runners.
tech_bullets: Other models: Cohere2MoE attention/MoE dual stream, single TP all-reduce and fused add + RMSNorm (1.14-1.36x TPOT, on by default, #62101). Beam TP all-reduce fused with norms and MoE finalize (#62366).
Speculative decoding: XPress (#54448), FLy (#53987), no draft-slot budget reservation for DFlash/DSpark (#59468), quantized draft `lm_head` (#59973), lookahead block hashes (#61589), MRV2 skipping.
Medusa and the MLP speculator were removed (#61701). The legacy Ray compiled-graph executor was removed and `VLLM_USE_RAY_V2_EXECUTOR_BACKEND` is gone; `RayExecutorV2` is the only Ray executor.
Transformers modeling backend: MTP speculative drafts (#61270), fused post-top-k MoE routers (#57410), graph caching instead of AOT caching (#58918) and dynamic-RoPE CUDA graphs (#58064).
technical_deep_dive.why_it_matters: Accelerates single-stream decode speed by 1.35x–2.2x using idle GPU memory bandwidth

technical_deep_dive.theme: Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups (DeepSeek-V4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3, MiniMax-M3)
technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v0.33.0, teams operating frontier moe & sparse-mla speedups relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on NVIDIA Blackwell (GB200/GB300/B200), Hopper (H100/H200), and multi-node Expert Parallel (EP) clusters.
tech_bullets: NVIDIA: Kimi-K3 and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash latency-specialized decode on GB300 (#61867, #61868). FA4 sparse MLA decode (#55866).
GLM: GLM-5.3-Flash defaults to an FP8 KV cache (9.8% higher end-to-end throughput in the PR's benchmark, #61228) and gets mHC TileLang decode kernels on Blackwell (#62745). GLM-5.3 per-token-group.
New defaults: GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 KV cache (#61228). lookahead block hashes for EAGLE/MTP prefix caching (#61589).

DeepSeek-V4 and V4.1: length-aware decode indexer block selection (about 850 us saved per step at 1M context, #61039). MegaMoE experts loaded directly in the DeepGEMM layout so `reload_weights` works.
technical_deep_dive.why_it_matters: Delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens

technical_deep_dive.theme: Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling (AMD ROCm 10 / MI355X, TPU & XPU)

# What's New in vLLM v0.33.0

## High-Level Explanation
vLLM v0.33.0 focuses on Next-Gen Speculative Decoding, Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups, and Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling. For operators, this release translates 44 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

## 1. What Are the High-Level Changes?
- **Next-Gen Speculative Decoding**: Improves next-gen speculative decoding for interactive coding assistants, agent loops, and low-batch-size real-time inference running on nvidia hopper/blackwell, amd mi300x/mi355x, and cpu/xpu draft runners, delivering accelerates single-stream decode speed by 1.35x–2.2x using idle GPU memory bandwidth.
- **Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups**: Improves frontier moe & sparse-mla speedups for frontier mixture-of-experts (moe) reasoning and agentic models (deepseek-v4/v4.1, glm-5.3, kimi-k3/k3.1, minimax-m3.1) running on nvidia blackwell (gb200/gb300/b200), hopper (h100/h200), and multi-node expert parallel (ep) clusters, delivering delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens.
- **Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling**: Improves multi-vendor accelerator scaling for cross-vendor llm fleets running deepseek, qwen, llama, and minimax outside cuda-only clouds running on amd instinct mi300x/mi350/mi355x (rocm 10.0), intel xpu, and google cloud tpu, delivering enables hardware price-performance arbitrage across AMD and NVIDIA GPU clouds without changing serving code.
- **Low-Precision Quantization Kernels**: Improves low-precision quantization kernels for 100b–1t+ parameter models (mistral large 4, deepseek-v4, qwen3.5/3.8) quantized to 4-bit/8-bit running on nvidia blackwell (sm100 nvfp4), hopper (sm90 fp8), and amd mi350/mi355x, delivering halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput.
- **Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend**: Improves day-0 model architectures, multimodal vision/audio & transformers backend for newly released foundation models, vision-language (vlm), speech/asr (`/v1/audio/transcriptions`), and multi-lora adapters running on standard single-node and multi-node gpu inference pools, delivering consolidates text, vision, speech, and embedding models onto a single unified vLLM serving fleet.

## 2. Who Benefits? (Models, GPUs & Your Bill)
| Workload / Team | Models / Services | GPUs / Hardware | Practical Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Next-Gen Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3, DSpark, DFlash, MTP & Suffix)** | Interactive coding assistants, agent loops, and low-batch-size real-time inference | NVIDIA Hopper/Blackwell, AMD MI300X/MI355X, and CPU/XPU draft runners | Accelerates single-stream decode speed by 1.35x–2.2x using idle GPU memory bandwidth |
| **Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups (DeepSeek-V4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3, MiniMax-M3)** | Frontier Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) reasoning and agentic models (DeepSeek-V4/V4.1, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3/K3.1, MiniMax-M3.1) | NVIDIA Blackwell (GB200/GB300/B200), Hopper (H100/H200), and multi-node Expert Parallel (EP) clusters | Delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens |
| **Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling (AMD ROCm 10 / MI355X, TPU & XPU)** | Cross-vendor LLM fleets running DeepSeek, Qwen, Llama, and MiniMax outside CUDA-only clouds | AMD Instinct MI300X/MI350/MI355X (ROCm 10.0), Intel XPU, and Google Cloud TPU | Enables hardware price-performance arbitrage across AMD and NVIDIA GPU clouds without changing serving code |
| **Low-Precision Quantization Kernels (NVFP4, MXFP4, MXFP8, FP8 & Humming)** | 100B–1T+ parameter models (Mistral Large 4, DeepSeek-V4, Qwen3.5/3.8) quantized to 4-bit/8-bit | NVIDIA Blackwell (SM100 NVFP4), Hopper (SM90 FP8), and AMD MI350/MI355X | Halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput |
| **Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend** | Newly released foundation models, Vision-Language (VLM), Speech/ASR (`/v1/audio/transcriptions`), and Multi-LoRA adapters | Standard single-node and multi-node GPU inference pools | Consolidates text, vision, speech, and embedding models onto a single unified vLLM serving fleet |
| **Model Runner V2 (MRV2) Consolidation & Breakable CUDA Graphs** | All production GPU deployments, latency-sensitive streaming apps, and custom logits processors | All CUDA and ROCm GPU fleets running vLLM's V2 execution engine | Cuts CPU dispatch overhead and lowers inter-token latency (ITL) by 3–15% while simplifying engine maintenance |
| **Extensible KV Cache, Memory Budgeting & Tiered Offloading** | High-concurrency chat APIs, long-context coding agents (32K–128K+), and multi-turn RAG workloads | NVIDIA Hopper (H100/H200), Blackwell (B200/GB200), and AMD Instinct (MI300X/MI355X) + host DRAM/NVMe tiers | Expands effective KV capacity by 25–55% per GPU, serving more concurrent users per rack without adding hardware |

## 3. What Does the Jargon Mean?
- **Extensible KV Cache**: Sizes the GPU Key-Value (KV) cache dynamically from actual free VRAM measured *after* model loading and CUDA graph warmup, rather than guessing via a static `gpu_memory_utilization` fraction. Why it matters: Unlocks 20–55% more KV token capacity per GPU (higher concurrency & throughput) without risking startup OOM crashes.
- **Model Runner V2 (MRV2)**: vLLM's redesigned GPU execution loop featuring persistent batching, zero-overhead input preparation, unified CUDA graph capture, and native speculative decoding. Why it matters: Replaces legacy Model Runner V1 as the sole GPU runner; lowers CPU-to-GPU launch overhead and unlocks higher token interactivity.
- **Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3 / DSpark / DFlash / MTP / Suffix)**: Uses a fast draft mechanism (a lightweight head like EAGLE3/DSpark, Multi-Token Prediction layers, or n-gram suffix matching) to propose multiple tokens at once, which the main model verifies in a single forward pass. Why it matters: Boosts per-user token generation speed (interactivity/TPOT) by 1.4x–2.5x without changing output quality.
- **MLA & Sparse-MLA (Multi-head Latent Attention)**: An attention architecture (used by DeepSeek-V3/V4, Kimi-K3, GLM-5) that compresses Key-Value states into a compact latent vector, optionally combined with sparse top-k token indexing. Why it matters: Slashes KV cache memory footprint on long contexts (32K–128K+), enabling far larger batch sizes per GPU.
- **NVFP4 / MXFP4 / FP8 Quantization**: 4-bit and 8-bit floating-point weight and activation formats accelerated natively by NVIDIA Blackwell/Hopper and AMD MI350/MI355X Tensor/Matrix cores. Why it matters: Nearly halves GPU memory vs. FP8 (and 4x vs. BF16) while up to doubling GEMM/MoE throughput on Blackwell and MI355X racks.
- **P/D Disaggregation (Prefill/Decode Split & NIXL)**: Separating compute-bound prompt processing (Prefill) onto one pool of GPUs and memory-bandwidth-bound token generation (Decode) onto another, transferring KV cache over RDMA/NVLink via NIXL. Why it matters: Stops long incoming prompts from stalling active streaming users, letting you tune GPU ratios independently for TTFT and TPOT SLAs.
- **DCP & PCP (Decode / Prefill Context Parallelism)**: Sharding the KV cache and attention computation of a single long-context sequence across multiple GPUs during prefill (PCP) or decode (DCP). Why it matters: Prevents single-GPU KV cache bottlenecks and reduces Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) on 32K–1M token agentic prompts.
- **MoE / MegaMoE & Expert Parallelism (EP / DeepGEMM)**: Specialized kernels and all-to-all communication schedules that route tokens across Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers distributed across many GPUs. Why it matters: Essential for serving frontier MoE models (DeepSeek-V4, Mistral Large 4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3) at high tokens/sec per GPU.
- **Piecewise & Breakable CUDA Graphs**: Capturing sequences of GPU kernel launches into replayable graphs (even across dynamic control flow) so the CPU doesn't launch hundreds of tiny kernels per token. Why it matters: Eliminates CPU bottlenecks during decode, cutting inter-token latency (ITL) by 5–25% without long `torch.compile` warmups.
- **TTFT (Time to First Token) & TPOT / ITL (Time Per Output Token)**: The two core LLM latency SLAs: TTFT measures how fast the first response token appears after a prompt; TPOT/ITL measures how fast subsequent tokens stream. Why it matters: Directly determines whether an AI coding agent or voice assistant feels snappy or sluggish to end users.
- **Tiered KV Offloading & Prefix Caching**: Evicting and reusing computed KV cache blocks across GPU HBM, host CPU DRAM, local NVMe, or shared object storage instead of recomputing shared system prompts. Why it matters: Dramatically lowers prefill compute cost and TTFT for multi-turn chat and agent workloads that share long context prefixes.

- **[Quantization]** Humming runs DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 MXFP4 experts as block FP8 on Hopper (#61875) and honors `--quantization-config.moe.activation` (#62751). pluggable KV cache data types (#52670). ([#61875](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61875), [#62751](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62751))
- **[Hardware & Performance]** CPU: zentorch 2.14.0.1 with float16 on Zen CPUs with AVX512-FP16 (#61411). MRV2 Triton warmup at startup removing an 11-20 s first-request compile (#62888). ([#61411](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61411), [#62888](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62888))
- **[Breaking Changes & Deprecations]** New defaults: GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 KV cache (#61228). lookahead block hashes for EAGLE/MTP prefix caching (#61589). ([#61228](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61228), [#61589](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61589))
- **[Large Scale Serving]** KV offload: CPU offload over up to 32 shm files (GLM-5.3 offload startup 63.6 s to 38.3 s, #59546), opt-in same-step small loads (#61961), EAGLE/MTP partial tails in align mode (#61019), lock/unlock and off-thread tiering (#58168), and many correctness fixes (#63266, #60810, #63652, #62929, #63010. - **[Model Support]** Kimi-K3: KDA RecoverSSM CuTe DSL verify/commit kernels on SM10x, with verify records moved out of the KV cache so KV connectors work (#63045); online quantization of NVIDIA projections (#62980). ([#63045](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63045), [#62980](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62980))

- **[Model Support]** New models: Reflection Beam-1.0 (`BeamForCausalLM`) day-0 support with its DFlash2 drafter and fused Blackwell kernels (#62074, #62042), plus `beam` reasoning and tool parsers (#62052). - **[Model Support]** Qwen: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next FP8 QSA KV cache on Ampere (#60602, #60992), packed NVFP4 PLE embeddings that fit Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 on one DGX Spark (#56273) and PLE short-conv prefill checkpoints (#61601); FlashInfer GDN prefill checkpoints for Qwen3-Next / Qwen3.5 (#60050). - **[Model Support]** Transformers modeling backend: MTP speculative drafts (#61270), fused post-top-k MoE routers (#57410), graph caching instead of AOT caching (#58918) and dynamic-RoPE CUDA graphs (#58064). - **[Engine Core]** Batch invariance: compressed-tensors W4A16/W8A16 (#60524), GateLinear routers (#59985), online FP8 MoE (#57092), and inductor batch-invariant mode under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` (#61118). ([#60524](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60524), [#59985](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59985))
- **[Large Scale Serving]** Context parallelism: MRV2 PCP decode full CUDA graphs (#62377). PCP for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with prefix caching and SWA bounded replay (#59857, #62183, #62384). ([#62377](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62377), [#59857](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59857))
- **[Large Scale Serving]** KV connectors: NIXL 1.5 strided descriptors (#61032), sleep mode with the pull connector (#59635), mixed hybrid MLA block sizes (#61002) and GQA draft head sharding (#58471). Mooncake sleep mode over RDMA (#59625) and Prometheus metrics (#56939). ([#61032](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61032), [#59635](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59635))

vllm_guides.positioning: vLLM v0.32.0 focuses on Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups, Low-Precision Quantization Kernels, and Model Runner V2. For operators, this release translates 55 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.
vllm_guides.high_level_explanation: vLLM v0.32.0 focuses on Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups, Low-Precision Quantization Kernels, and Model Runner V2. For operators, this release translates 55 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.
vllm_guides.verdict: UPGRADE WITH CONFIG CHECK — High-ROI throughput/stability gains, but review breaking flag/API removals first

high_level_changes.headline: Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves frontier moe & sparse-mla speedups for frontier mixture-of-experts (moe) reasoning and agentic models (deepseek-v4/v4.1, glm-5.3, kimi-k3/k3.1, minimax-m3.1) running on nvidia blackwell (gb200/gb300/b200), hopper (h100/h200), and multi-node expert parallel (ep) clusters, delivering delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens.

high_level_changes.headline: Low-Precision Quantization Kernels
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves low-precision quantization kernels for 100b–1t+ parameter models (mistral large 4, deepseek-v4, qwen3.5/3.8) quantized to 4-bit/8-bit running on nvidia blackwell (sm100 nvfp4), hopper (sm90 fp8), and amd mi350/mi355x, delivering halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput.

high_level_changes.headline: Model Runner V2
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves model runner v2 for all production gpu deployments, latency-sensitive streaming apps, and custom logits processors running on all cuda and rocm gpu fleets running vllm's v2 execution engine, delivering cuts CPU dispatch overhead and lowers inter-token latency (ITL) by 3–15% while simplifying engine maintenance.

high_level_changes.headline: Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves multi-vendor accelerator scaling for cross-vendor llm fleets running deepseek, qwen, llama, and minimax outside cuda-only clouds running on amd instinct mi300x/mi350/mi355x (rocm 10.0), intel xpu, and google cloud tpu, delivering enables hardware price-performance arbitrage across AMD and NVIDIA GPU clouds without changing serving code.

high_level_changes.headline: Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves day-0 model architectures, multimodal vision/audio & transformers backend for newly released foundation models, vision-language (vlm), speech/asr (`/v1/audio/transcriptions`), and multi-lora adapters running on standard single-node and multi-node gpu inference pools, delivering consolidates text, vision, speech, and embedding models onto a single unified vLLM serving fleet.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Sizes the GPU Key-Value (KV) cache dynamically from actual free VRAM measured *after* model loading and CUDA graph warmup, rather than guessing via a static `gpu_memory_utilization` fraction.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Unlocks 20–55% more KV token capacity per GPU (higher concurrency & throughput) without risking startup OOM crashes.

jargon_glossary.meaning: vLLM's redesigned GPU execution loop featuring persistent batching, zero-overhead input preparation, unified CUDA graph capture, and native speculative decoding.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Replaces legacy Model Runner V1 as the sole GPU runner; lowers CPU-to-GPU launch overhead and unlocks higher token interactivity.

jargon_glossary.term: Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3 / DSpark / DFlash / MTP / Suffix)
jargon_glossary.meaning: Uses a fast draft mechanism (a lightweight head like EAGLE3/DSpark, Multi-Token Prediction layers, or n-gram suffix matching) to propose multiple tokens at once, which the main model verifies in a single forward pass.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Boosts per-user token generation speed (interactivity/TPOT) by 1.4x–2.5x without changing output quality.

jargon_glossary.meaning: An attention architecture (used by DeepSeek-V3/V4, Kimi-K3, GLM-5) that compresses Key-Value states into a compact latent vector, optionally combined with sparse top-k token indexing.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Slashes KV cache memory footprint on long contexts (32K–128K+), enabling far larger batch sizes per GPU.

jargon_glossary.meaning: 4-bit and 8-bit floating-point weight and activation formats accelerated natively by NVIDIA Blackwell/Hopper and AMD MI350/MI355X Tensor/Matrix cores.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Nearly halves GPU memory vs. FP8 (and 4x vs. BF16) while up to doubling GEMM/MoE throughput on Blackwell and MI355X racks.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Separating compute-bound prompt processing (Prefill) onto one pool of GPUs and memory-bandwidth-bound token generation (Decode) onto another, transferring KV cache over RDMA/NVLink via NIXL.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Stops long incoming prompts from stalling active streaming users, letting you tune GPU ratios independently for TTFT and TPOT SLAs.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Sharding the KV cache and attention computation of a single long-context sequence across multiple GPUs during prefill (PCP) or decode (DCP).
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Prevents single-GPU KV cache bottlenecks and reduces Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) on 32K–1M token agentic prompts.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Specialized kernels and all-to-all communication schedules that route tokens across Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers distributed across many GPUs.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Essential for serving frontier MoE models (DeepSeek-V4, Mistral Large 4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3) at high tokens/sec per GPU.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Capturing sequences of GPU kernel launches into replayable graphs (even across dynamic control flow) so the CPU doesn't launch hundreds of tiny kernels per token.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Eliminates CPU bottlenecks during decode, cutting inter-token latency (ITL) by 5–25% without long `torch.compile` warmups.

jargon_glossary.term: TTFT (Time to First Token) & TPOT / ITL (Time Per Output Token)
jargon_glossary.meaning: The two core LLM latency SLAs: TTFT measures how fast the first response token appears after a prompt; TPOT/ITL measures how fast subsequent tokens stream.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Directly determines whether an AI coding agent or voice assistant feels snappy or sluggish to end users.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Evicting and reusing computed KV cache blocks across GPU HBM, host CPU DRAM, local NVMe, or shared object storage instead of recomputing shared system prompts.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Dramatically lowers prefill compute cost and TTFT for multi-turn chat and agent workloads that share long context prefixes.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Compiling vLLM's custom C++/CUDA kernels against PyTorch's binary-stable application interface rather than internal C++ symbols.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Lets you upgrade PyTorch versions or security patches without rebuilding vLLM's entire CUDA kernel suite from source.

should_i_upgrade.text: Python 3.10 is no longer supported; the minimum is Python 3.11 (#60402). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading
Default CORS origins changed from `*` to none; set `--allowed-origins` for browser clients (#61009). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading
`transformers>=5.16.1,<5.20.0` and `tokenizers>=0.23.2` are required (#57387, #59796). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading

The torch.compile sequence parallelism and AsyncTP passes were removed, along with `PassConfig.enable_sp`, `fuse_gemm_comms` and `sp_min_token_num`; model-level sequence parallelism is unaffected (#60517). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading
Cascade attention was removed; `--disable-cascade-attn` still parses but only warns and will be removed in v0.33.0 (#61126). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading
`mamba_cache_mode="all"` was removed; `--mamba-cache-mode all` now fails validation (#58997). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading

Previously deprecated APIs were removed: `wait_for_inflight_requests` (use `mode="wait"`), `AsyncLLM.pause_generation()`, `IOProcessor.output_to_response`, `vllm.scripts.main()` and `vllm bench throughput --dataset` (#60923). The `sonnet` benchmark dataset was removed as scheduled (#60129). Tensorizer support was removed from LoRA (#60024), and the PyO3 `vllm._rust_tool_parser` bridge was removed (#59744). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading

API changes: `max_tokens` is treated as an upper bound on output rather than reserved from the context window (#57035); Responses API streaming uses `response.content_part.added/done` with `part.type="reasoning_text"` instead of `response.reasoning_part.added/done` (#59652); `SamplingParams.prompt_logprob_token_ids` is per row (#56984); `/inference/v1/generate` logprobs use integer token IDs (#58181); sleep API responses are standardized and invalid levels return 400 (#52864); `return_mm_kwargs` is deprecated in favor of `mm_payload` (#61427). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading

Watermarking: when the engine has watermarking configured, an omitted request field means enabled and only `false` opts out; unsupported combinations warn and fall back (#56801). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading
Rust frontend: `qwen3_xml` now parses Qwen3-Coder XML (alias of `qwen3_coder`); use the new `qwen3_json` for the JSON format (#60136). -> Action: Verify compatibility before upgrading

# What's New in vLLM v0.32.0

## High-Level Explanation
vLLM v0.32.0 focuses on Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups, Low-Precision Quantization Kernels, and Model Runner V2. For operators, this release translates 55 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

## 1. What Are the High-Level Changes?
- **Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups**: Improves frontier moe & sparse-mla speedups for frontier mixture-of-experts (moe) reasoning and agentic models (deepseek-v4/v4.1, glm-5.3, kimi-k3/k3.1, minimax-m3.1) running on nvidia blackwell (gb200/gb300/b200), hopper (h100/h200), and multi-node expert parallel (ep) clusters, delivering delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens.
- **Low-Precision Quantization Kernels**: Improves low-precision quantization kernels for 100b–1t+ parameter models (mistral large 4, deepseek-v4, qwen3.5/3.8) quantized to 4-bit/8-bit running on nvidia blackwell (sm100 nvfp4), hopper (sm90 fp8), and amd mi350/mi355x, delivering halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput.
- **Model Runner V2**: Improves model runner v2 for all production gpu deployments, latency-sensitive streaming apps, and custom logits processors running on all cuda and rocm gpu fleets running vllm's v2 execution engine, delivering cuts CPU dispatch overhead and lowers inter-token latency (ITL) by 3–15% while simplifying engine maintenance.
- **Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling**: Improves multi-vendor accelerator scaling for cross-vendor llm fleets running deepseek, qwen, llama, and minimax outside cuda-only clouds running on amd instinct mi300x/mi350/mi355x (rocm 10.0), intel xpu, and google cloud tpu, delivering enables hardware price-performance arbitrage across AMD and NVIDIA GPU clouds without changing serving code.
- **Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend**: Improves day-0 model architectures, multimodal vision/audio & transformers backend for newly released foundation models, vision-language (vlm), speech/asr (`/v1/audio/transcriptions`), and multi-lora adapters running on standard single-node and multi-node gpu inference pools, delivering consolidates text, vision, speech, and embedding models onto a single unified vLLM serving fleet.

## 3. What Does the Jargon Mean?
- **Extensible KV Cache**: Sizes the GPU Key-Value (KV) cache dynamically from actual free VRAM measured *after* model loading and CUDA graph warmup, rather than guessing via a static `gpu_memory_utilization` fraction. Why it matters: Unlocks 20–55% more KV token capacity per GPU (higher concurrency & throughput) without risking startup OOM crashes.
- **Model Runner V2 (MRV2)**: vLLM's redesigned GPU execution loop featuring persistent batching, zero-overhead input preparation, unified CUDA graph capture, and native speculative decoding. Why it matters: Replaces legacy Model Runner V1 as the sole GPU runner; lowers CPU-to-GPU launch overhead and unlocks higher token interactivity.
- **Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3 / DSpark / DFlash / MTP / Suffix)**: Uses a fast draft mechanism (a lightweight head like EAGLE3/DSpark, Multi-Token Prediction layers, or n-gram suffix matching) to propose multiple tokens at once, which the main model verifies in a single forward pass. Why it matters: Boosts per-user token generation speed (interactivity/TPOT) by 1.4x–2.5x without changing output quality.
- **MLA & Sparse-MLA (Multi-head Latent Attention)**: An attention architecture (used by DeepSeek-V3/V4, Kimi-K3, GLM-5) that compresses Key-Value states into a compact latent vector, optionally combined with sparse top-k token indexing. Why it matters: Slashes KV cache memory footprint on long contexts (32K–128K+), enabling far larger batch sizes per GPU.
- **NVFP4 / MXFP4 / FP8 Quantization**: 4-bit and 8-bit floating-point weight and activation formats accelerated natively by NVIDIA Blackwell/Hopper and AMD MI350/MI355X Tensor/Matrix cores. Why it matters: Nearly halves GPU memory vs. FP8 (and 4x vs. BF16) while up to doubling GEMM/MoE throughput on Blackwell and MI355X racks.
- **P/D Disaggregation (Prefill/Decode Split & NIXL)**: Separating compute-bound prompt processing (Prefill) onto one pool of GPUs and memory-bandwidth-bound token generation (Decode) onto another, transferring KV cache over RDMA/NVLink via NIXL. Why it matters: Stops long incoming prompts from stalling active streaming users, letting you tune GPU ratios independently for TTFT and TPOT SLAs.
- **DCP & PCP (Decode / Prefill Context Parallelism)**: Sharding the KV cache and attention computation of a single long-context sequence across multiple GPUs during prefill (PCP) or decode (DCP). Why it matters: Prevents single-GPU KV cache bottlenecks and reduces Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) on 32K–1M token agentic prompts.
- **MoE / MegaMoE & Expert Parallelism (EP / DeepGEMM)**: Specialized kernels and all-to-all communication schedules that route tokens across Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers distributed across many GPUs. Why it matters: Essential for serving frontier MoE models (DeepSeek-V4, Mistral Large 4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3) at high tokens/sec per GPU.
- **Piecewise & Breakable CUDA Graphs**: Capturing sequences of GPU kernel launches into replayable graphs (even across dynamic control flow) so the CPU doesn't launch hundreds of tiny kernels per token. Why it matters: Eliminates CPU bottlenecks during decode, cutting inter-token latency (ITL) by 5–25% without long `torch.compile` warmups.
- **TTFT (Time to First Token) & TPOT / ITL (Time Per Output Token)**: The two core LLM latency SLAs: TTFT measures how fast the first response token appears after a prompt; TPOT/ITL measures how fast subsequent tokens stream. Why it matters: Directly determines whether an AI coding agent or voice assistant feels snappy or sluggish to end users.
- **Tiered KV Offloading & Prefix Caching**: Evicting and reusing computed KV cache blocks across GPU HBM, host CPU DRAM, local NVMe, or shared object storage instead of recomputing shared system prompts. Why it matters: Dramatically lowers prefill compute cost and TTFT for multi-turn chat and agent workloads that share long context prefixes.
- **LibTorch Stable ABI**: Compiling vLLM's custom C++/CUDA kernels against PyTorch's binary-stable application interface rather than internal C++ symbols. Why it matters: Lets you upgrade PyTorch versions or security patches without rebuilding vLLM's entire CUDA kernel suite from source.

([#50300](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50300))

For operators, this release translates 56 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

high_level_changes.headline: Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves frontier moe & sparse-mla speedups for frontier mixture-of-experts (moe) reasoning and agentic models (deepseek-v4/v4.1, glm-5.3, kimi-k3/k3.1, minimax-m3.1) running on nvidia blackwell (gb200/gb300/b200), hopper (h100/h200), and multi-node expert parallel (ep) clusters, delivering delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens.

high_level_changes.headline: Model Runner V2
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves model runner v2 for all production gpu deployments, latency-sensitive streaming apps, and custom logits processors running on all cuda and rocm gpu fleets running vllm's v2 execution engine, delivering cuts CPU dispatch overhead and lowers inter-token latency (ITL) by 3–15% while simplifying engine maintenance.

high_level_changes.headline: Low-Precision Quantization Kernels
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves low-precision quantization kernels for 100b–1t+ parameter models (mistral large 4, deepseek-v4, qwen3.5/3.8) quantized to 4-bit/8-bit running on nvidia blackwell (sm100 nvfp4), hopper (sm90 fp8), and amd mi350/mi355x, delivering halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput.

high_level_changes.headline: Next-Gen Speculative Decoding
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves next-gen speculative decoding for interactive coding assistants, agent loops, and low-batch-size real-time inference running on nvidia hopper/blackwell, amd mi300x/mi355x, and cpu/xpu draft runners, delivering accelerates single-stream decode speed by 1.35x–2.2x using idle GPU memory bandwidth.

high_level_changes.headline: Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves multi-vendor accelerator scaling for cross-vendor llm fleets running deepseek, qwen, llama, and minimax outside cuda-only clouds running on amd instinct mi300x/mi350/mi355x (rocm 10.0), intel xpu, and google cloud tpu, delivering enables hardware price-performance arbitrage across AMD and NVIDIA GPU clouds without changing serving code.
