# What's New in Kubernetes v1.6

## High-Level Explanation
Kubernetes v1.6 focuses on Feature Enhancements, Urgent Upgrade Notes Enhancements, and StatefulSet PVC Auto-Cleanup, Volume Health & Storage Expansion. For operators, this release translates 511 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

## 1. What Are the High-Level Changes?
- **Feature Enhancements**: Improves feature enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.
- **Urgent Upgrade Notes Enhancements**: Improves urgent upgrade notes enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.
- **StatefulSet PVC Auto-Cleanup, Volume Health & Storage Expansion**: Improves statefulset pvc auto-cleanup, volume health & storage expansion for databases, kafka/clickhouse clusters, and stateful ai checkpoint storage running on csi storage drivers and cloud block volumes, delivering eliminates orphaned cloud disk charges when scaling down or deleting temporary StatefulSets.
- **Networking, `nftables` Proxy & Traffic Observability**: Improves networking, `nftables` proxy & traffic observability for high-throughput east-west microservices and latency-sensitive ingress traffic running on linux dataplane (`nftables`/`ipvs`) and cloud load balancers, delivering lowers cross-AZ data transfer costs (`trafficDistribution`) and reduces node CPU spent on iptables rules.
- **CEL-Based Validating & Mutating Admission Policies**: Improves cel-based validating & mutating admission policies for platform security guardrails, multi-tenant compliance policies, and default resource injectors running on in-process `kube-apiserver` admission chain (replaces external webhook deployments), delivering removes dedicated webhook pods and eliminates deployment outages caused by webhook timeouts.

## 2. Who Benefits? (Models, GPUs & Your Bill)
| Workload / Team | Models / Services | GPUs / Hardware | Practical Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Feature Enhancements** | General platform workloads and API consumers | Standard cluster nodes and runtime components | Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil |
| **Urgent Upgrade Notes Enhancements** | General platform workloads and API consumers | Standard cluster nodes and runtime components | Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil |
| **StatefulSet PVC Auto-Cleanup, Volume Health & Storage Expansion** | Databases, Kafka/ClickHouse clusters, and stateful AI checkpoint storage | CSI storage drivers and cloud block volumes | Eliminates orphaned cloud disk charges when scaling down or deleting temporary StatefulSets |
| **Networking, `nftables` Proxy & Traffic Observability** | High-throughput east-west microservices and latency-sensitive ingress traffic | Linux dataplane (`nftables`/`ipvs`) and cloud load balancers | Lowers cross-AZ data transfer costs (`trafficDistribution`) and reduces node CPU spent on iptables rules |
| **CEL-Based Validating & Mutating Admission Policies** | Platform security guardrails, multi-tenant compliance policies, and default resource injectors | In-process `kube-apiserver` admission chain (replaces external webhook deployments) | Removes dedicated webhook pods and eliminates deployment outages caused by webhook timeouts |
| **API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale** | Operator-heavy platforms, Argo CD / Flux GitOps controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ CRDs/Pods | Control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) CPU and memory footprint | Cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages |
| **Workload-Aware & Gang Scheduling (`PodGroup` / `Job` / Queueing)** | Distributed AI training, multi-node batch jobs, Ray/Spark clusters, and MPI workloads | High-density GPU/CPU batch pools and `kube-scheduler` queues | Prevents partial-allocation deadlocks where expensive GPU nodes sit idle waiting for peer workers |

## 3. What Does the Jargon Mean?
- **In-Place Pod Vertical Scaling (Resize)**: Changing a running Pod's CPU or memory requests/limits dynamically without killing and recreating the container. Why it matters: Eliminates cold-start restarts and dropped connections when scaling stateful services, databases, or warm AI model servers.
- **Gang Scheduling (`Workload` / `PodGroup`)**: An 'all-or-nothing' scheduling guarantee where a group of cooperating Pods (like a multi-node training or distributed inference job) only starts when capacity exists for the entire group. Why it matters: Prevents expensive GPUs from sitting idle in deadlocked partial allocations when a cluster is near capacity.
- **ValidatingAdmissionPolicy & MutatingAdmissionPolicy (CEL)**: In-process policy rules written in Common Expression Language (CEL) evaluated directly inside `kube-apiserver` without calling external admission webhook servers. Why it matters: Removes webhook network latency and prevents a crashed policy pod from taking down cluster deployments.
- **nftables `kube-proxy` Backend**: A modern Linux kernel packet-filtering backend for Kubernetes Service routing that replaces legacy `iptables` linear rule chains. Why it matters: Cuts Service rule programming latency and CPU overhead on clusters with tens of thousands of Services.
- **HPA Scale-to-Zero (`minReplicas: 0`)**: Allows `HorizontalPodAutoscaler` to scale external/queue-driven workloads all the way down to 0 replicas when idle and wake them when queue depth rises. Why it matters: Directly cuts cloud compute and GPU bills for bursty batch/inference workers during off-peak hours.
- **CSI (Container Storage Interface)**: The standard plugin layer connecting Kubernetes PersistentVolumes to cloud block/file storage providers. Why it matters: Controls how fast stateful workloads attach disks, recover from node failures, and handle credentials.

## 4. Should I Upgrade?
**Verdict**: UPGRADE WITH CONFIG CHECK — High-ROI throughput/stability gains, but review breaking flag/API removals first
- **Urgent Upgrade Notes**: Certificates API: * Users of the alpha certificates API should delete v1alpha1 CSRs from the API before upgrading and recreate them as v1beta1 CSR after upgrading.. ([#39772](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/39772))
- **Urgent Upgrade Notes**: Cluster Autoscaler: * If you are using (or planning to use) Cluster Autoscaler please wait for Kubernetes 1.6.1. In 1.6.0 Cluster Autoscaler may occasionally increase the size of the cluster a bit more than it. (Upstream release notes)
- **Urgent Upgrade Notes**: Deployment now fully respects ControllerRef to avoid fighting over Pods and ReplicaSets. At the time of upgrade, you must not have Deployments with selectors that overlap, or else [ownership of ReplicaSets may. ([#42175](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/42175))
- **Urgent Upgrade Notes**: Federation: * The --dns-provider argument of 'kubefed init' is now mandatory and does not default to `google-clouddns`. To initialize a Federation control plane with Google Cloud DNS, use the following. ([#42092](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/42092))
- **Urgent Upgrade Notes**: Federation: * Cluster federation servers have changed the location in etcd where federated services are stored, so existing federated services must be deleted and recreated. Before upgrading, export all. ([#37770](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/37770))
- **Urgent Upgrade Notes**: Internal Storage Layer: * upgrade to etcd3 prior to upgrading to 1.6 OR explicitly specify `--storage-backend=etcd2 --storage-media-type=application/json` when starting the apiserver. (Upstream release notes)
- **Urgent Upgrade Notes**: Node Components: * Kubelet with the Docker-CRI implementation. (Upstream release notes)
- **Urgent Upgrade Notes**: Node Components:   * The Docker-CRI implementation is enabled by default. (Upstream release notes)

kubernetes_guides.positioning: Kubernetes v1.5 focuses on Feature Enhancements, Urgent Upgrade Notes Enhancements, and StatefulSet PVC Auto-Cleanup, Volume Health & Storage Expansion. For operators, this release translates 98 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

high_level_changes.headline: Feature Enhancements
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves feature enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.

high_level_changes.headline: Urgent Upgrade Notes Enhancements
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves urgent upgrade notes enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.

high_level_changes.headline: StatefulSet PVC Auto-Cleanup, Volume Health & Storage Expansion
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves statefulset pvc auto-cleanup, volume health & storage expansion for databases, kafka/clickhouse clusters, and stateful ai checkpoint storage running on csi storage drivers and cloud block volumes, delivering eliminates orphaned cloud disk charges when scaling down or deleting temporary StatefulSets.

high_level_changes.headline: API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves api server & etcd watch/cache efficiency at scale for operator-heavy platforms, argo cd / flux gitops controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ crds/pods running on control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) cpu and memory footprint, delivering cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages.

high_level_changes.headline: Autoscaling & Scale-to-Zero Cost Optimization
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves autoscaling & scale-to-zero cost optimization for event-driven workers, async queue consumers, and bursty gpu inference endpoints running on autoscaled node pools (karpenter / cluster autoscaler) and hpa controller, delivering directly saves compute spend by parking idle worker pools at 0 replicas until queue demand arrives.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Kubernetes' next-generation API (`resource.k8s.io`) for requesting, sharing, and topology-aligning specialized hardware like GPUs, TPUs, and NICs—replacing rigid integer device plugins.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Lets multiple pods share fractional GPUs safely or co-schedule across NVLink domains without custom vendor hacks.

jargon_glossary.meaning: An 'all-or-nothing' scheduling guarantee where a group of cooperating Pods (like a multi-node training or distributed inference job) only starts when capacity exists for the entire group.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Prevents expensive GPUs from sitting idle in deadlocked partial allocations when a cluster is near capacity.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Maps the `root` user inside a container to an unprivileged non-root UID on the host node kernel.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Dramatically reduces container-escape blast radius even for legacy workloads that require running as `root` inside the container.

jargon_glossary.meaning: The standard plugin layer connecting Kubernetes PersistentVolumes to cloud block/file storage providers.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Controls how fast stateful workloads attach disks, recover from node failures, and handle credentials.

should_i_upgrade.text: CRI [known issues and limitations](https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/devel/sig-node/container-runtime-interface.md#kubernetes-v15-release-cri-v1alpha1)
getDeviceNameFromMount() function doesn't return the volume path correctly when the volume path contains spaces [#37712](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/37712)
Federation alpha features do not have feature gates defined and are hence enabled by default. This will be fixed in a future release. [#38593](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/38593)

Federation control plane can be upgraded by updating the image fields in the `Deployment` specs of the control plane components. However, federation control plane upgrades were not tested in this release [38537](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/38537)
Important Security-related changes before upgrading

You *MUST* set `--anonymous-auth=false` flag on your kube-apiserver unless you are a developer testing this feature and understand it. If you do not, you risk allowing unauthorized users to access your apiserver.

You *MUST* set `--anonymous-auth=false` flag on your federation apiserver unless you are a developer testing this feature and understand it. If you do not, you risk allowing unauthorized users to access your federation apiserver.
You do not need to adjust this flag on Kubelet:  there was no authorization for the Kubelet APIs in 1.4.
batch/v2alpha1.ScheduledJob has been renamed, use batch/v2alpha1.CronJob instead ([#36021](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/36021), [@soltysh](https://github.com/soltysh))

PetSet has been renamed to StatefulSet. If you have existing PetSets, **you must perform extra migration steps** both before and after upgrading to convert them to StatefulSets. ([docs](http://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/manage-stateful-set/upgrade-pet-set-to-stateful-set/)) ([#35663](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/35663), [@janetkuo](https://github.com/janetkuo))

technical_deep_dive.theme: Feature Enhancements
technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v1.5, teams operating feature enhancements relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on Standard cluster nodes and runtime components.
tech_bullets: `kubectl apply` is now able to delete resources you no longer need with `--prune` ([kubernetes/features#128](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/128)).
Enable DNS Horizontal Autoscaling with beta ConfigMap parameters support ([docs](http://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/administer-cluster/dns-horizontal-autoscaling/)).
In order to preserve safety guarantees the cluster no longer force deletes pods on un-responsive nodes and users are now warned if they try to force delete pods via the CLI. (#119).
Added ability to create/remove clusters w/highly available (replicated) masters on GCE using kube-up/kube-down scripts. ([docs](http://kubernetes.io/docs/admin/ha-master-gce/)).

The deprecated kubelet --configure-cbr0 flag has been removed, and with that the "classic" networking mode as well.  If you depend on this mode, please investigate whether the other network plugins (#34906).
The deprecated kube-scheduler --bind-pods-qps and --bind-pods burst flags have been removed, use --kube-api-qps and --kube-api-burst instead (#34471).
Federation control plane can be upgraded by updating the image fields in the `Deployment` specs of the control plane components. However, federation control plane upgrades were not tested in this.

# What's New in Kubernetes v1.5

## High-Level Explanation
Kubernetes v1.5 focuses on Feature Enhancements, Urgent Upgrade Notes Enhancements, and StatefulSet PVC Auto-Cleanup, Volume Health & Storage Expansion. For operators, this release translates 98 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

## 1. What Are the High-Level Changes?
- **Feature Enhancements**: Improves feature enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.
- **Urgent Upgrade Notes Enhancements**: Improves urgent upgrade notes enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.
- **StatefulSet PVC Auto-Cleanup, Volume Health & Storage Expansion**: Improves statefulset pvc auto-cleanup, volume health & storage expansion for databases, kafka/clickhouse clusters, and stateful ai checkpoint storage running on csi storage drivers and cloud block volumes, delivering eliminates orphaned cloud disk charges when scaling down or deleting temporary StatefulSets.
- **API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale**: Improves api server & etcd watch/cache efficiency at scale for operator-heavy platforms, argo cd / flux gitops controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ crds/pods running on control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) cpu and memory footprint, delivering cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages.
- **Autoscaling & Scale-to-Zero Cost Optimization**: Improves autoscaling & scale-to-zero cost optimization for event-driven workers, async queue consumers, and bursty gpu inference endpoints running on autoscaled node pools (karpenter / cluster autoscaler) and hpa controller, delivering directly saves compute spend by parking idle worker pools at 0 replicas until queue demand arrives.

## 2. Who Benefits? (Models, GPUs & Your Bill)
| Workload / Team | Models / Services | GPUs / Hardware | Practical Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Feature Enhancements** | General platform workloads and API consumers | Standard cluster nodes and runtime components | Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil |
| **Urgent Upgrade Notes Enhancements** | General platform workloads and API consumers | Standard cluster nodes and runtime components | Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil |
| **StatefulSet PVC Auto-Cleanup, Volume Health & Storage Expansion** | Databases, Kafka/ClickHouse clusters, and stateful AI checkpoint storage | CSI storage drivers and cloud block volumes | Eliminates orphaned cloud disk charges when scaling down or deleting temporary StatefulSets |
| **API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale** | Operator-heavy platforms, Argo CD / Flux GitOps controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ CRDs/Pods | Control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) CPU and memory footprint | Cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages |
| **Autoscaling & Scale-to-Zero Cost Optimization** | Event-driven workers, async queue consumers, and bursty GPU inference endpoints | Autoscaled node pools (Karpenter / Cluster Autoscaler) and HPA controller | Directly saves compute spend by parking idle worker pools at 0 replicas until queue demand arrives |
| **Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) & GPU/Accelerator Management** | AI/ML training, LLM inference pods, fractional/multi-GPU workloads, and NIC/FPGA consumers | NVIDIA/AMD GPU nodes, multi-NIC RDMA clusters, and topology-aware hardware pools | Higher GPU utilization and fewer stranded accelerators via standardized device sharing and health reporting |
| **Workload Identity, User Namespaces & Fine-Grained Authz** | Multi-tenant SaaS workloads, zero-trust service meshes, and privileged container migrations | Linux kernel namespaces, kubelet endpoints, and CSI secret injection paths | Reduces security agent/sidecar overhead and shrinks blast radius of container compromises |

## 3. What Does the Jargon Mean?
- **DRA (Dynamic Resource Allocation)**: Kubernetes' next-generation API (`resource.k8s.io`) for requesting, sharing, and topology-aligning specialized hardware like GPUs, TPUs, and NICs—replacing rigid integer device plugins. Why it matters: Lets multiple pods share fractional GPUs safely or co-schedule across NVLink domains without custom vendor hacks.
- **Gang Scheduling (`Workload` / `PodGroup`)**: An 'all-or-nothing' scheduling guarantee where a group of cooperating Pods (like a multi-node training or distributed inference job) only starts when capacity exists for the entire group. Why it matters: Prevents expensive GPUs from sitting idle in deadlocked partial allocations when a cluster is near capacity.
- **Linux User Namespaces (`hostUsers: false`)**: Maps the `root` user inside a container to an unprivileged non-root UID on the host node kernel. Why it matters: Dramatically reduces container-escape blast radius even for legacy workloads that require running as `root` inside the container.
- **CSI (Container Storage Interface)**: The standard plugin layer connecting Kubernetes PersistentVolumes to cloud block/file storage providers. Why it matters: Controls how fast stateful workloads attach disks, recover from node failures, and handle credentials.

## 4. Should I Upgrade?
**Verdict**: UPGRADE WITH CONFIG CHECK — High-ROI throughput/stability gains, but review breaking flag/API removals first
- **Urgent Upgrade Notes**: CRI [known issues and limitations](https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/devel/sig-node/container-runtime-interface.md#kubernetes-v15-release-cri-v1alpha1). (Upstream release notes)
- **Urgent Upgrade Notes**: getDeviceNameFromMount() function doesn't return the volume path correctly when the volume path contains spaces [#37712](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/37712). ([#37712](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/37712))
- **Urgent Upgrade Notes**: Federation alpha features do not have feature gates defined and are hence enabled by default. This will be fixed in a future release. [#38593](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/38593). ([#38593](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/38593))
- **Urgent Upgrade Notes**: Federation control plane can be upgraded by updating the image fields in the `Deployment` specs of the control plane components. However, federation control plane upgrades were not tested in this release. (Upstream release notes)
- **Urgent Upgrade Notes**: Important Security-related changes before upgrading. (Upstream release notes)
- **Urgent Upgrade Notes**: You *MUST* set `--anonymous-auth=false` flag on your kube-apiserver unless you are a developer testing this feature and understand it. If you do not, you risk allowing unauthorized users to access your. (Upstream release notes)
- **Urgent Upgrade Notes**: You *MUST* set `--anonymous-auth=false` flag on your federation apiserver unless you are a developer testing this feature and understand it. If you do not, you risk allowing unauthorized users to access your. (Upstream release notes)
- **Urgent Upgrade Notes**: You do not need to adjust this flag on Kubelet:  there was no authorization for the Kubelet APIs in 1.4. (Upstream release notes)
- **Urgent Upgrade Notes**: batch/v2alpha1.ScheduledJob has been renamed, use batch/v2alpha1.CronJob instead ([#36021](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/36021), [@soltysh](https://github.com/soltysh)). ([#36021](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/36021))

high_level_changes.headline: Feature Enhancements
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves feature enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.

high_level_changes.headline: Urgent Upgrade Notes Enhancements
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves urgent upgrade notes enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.

high_level_changes.headline: API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves api server & etcd watch/cache efficiency at scale for operator-heavy platforms, argo cd / flux gitops controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ crds/pods running on control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) cpu and memory footprint, delivering cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages.

high_level_changes.headline: Networking, `nftables` Proxy & Traffic Observability
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves networking, `nftables` proxy & traffic observability for high-throughput east-west microservices and latency-sensitive ingress traffic running on linux dataplane (`nftables`/`ipvs`) and cloud load balancers, delivering lowers cross-AZ data transfer costs (`trafficDistribution`) and reduces node CPU spent on iptables rules.

high_level_changes.headline: Workload-Aware & Gang Scheduling
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves workload-aware & gang scheduling for distributed ai training, multi-node batch jobs, ray/spark clusters, and mpi workloads running on high-density gpu/cpu batch pools and `kube-scheduler` queues, delivering prevents partial-allocation deadlocks where expensive GPU nodes sit idle waiting for peer workers.

jargon_glossary.meaning: An 'all-or-nothing' scheduling guarantee where a group of cooperating Pods (like a multi-node training or distributed inference job) only starts when capacity exists for the entire group.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Prevents expensive GPUs from sitting idle in deadlocked partial allocations when a cluster is near capacity.

jargon_glossary.meaning: In-process policy rules written in Common Expression Language (CEL) evaluated directly inside `kube-apiserver` without calling external admission webhook servers.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Removes webhook network latency and prevents a crashed policy pod from taking down cluster deployments.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Maps the `root` user inside a container to an unprivileged non-root UID on the host node kernel.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Dramatically reduces container-escape blast radius even for legacy workloads that require running as `root` inside the container.

jargon_glossary.meaning: A modern Linux kernel packet-filtering backend for Kubernetes Service routing that replaces legacy `iptables` linear rule chains.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Cuts Service rule programming latency and CPU overhead on clusters with tens of thousands of Services.

[alpha] Creating a `Federated Ingress` is as simple as submitting an `Ingress` creation request to the Federation API Server. kubernetes_guides.markdown:
# What's New in Kubernetes v1.4

## High-Level Explanation
Kubernetes v1.4 focuses on Feature Enhancements, Urgent Upgrade Notes Enhancements, and API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale. For operators, this release translates 82 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

## 1. What Are the High-Level Changes?
- **Feature Enhancements**: Improves feature enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.
- **Urgent Upgrade Notes Enhancements**: Improves urgent upgrade notes enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.
- **API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale**: Improves api server & etcd watch/cache efficiency at scale for operator-heavy platforms, argo cd / flux gitops controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ crds/pods running on control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) cpu and memory footprint, delivering cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages.
- **Networking, `nftables` Proxy & Traffic Observability**: Improves networking, `nftables` proxy & traffic observability for high-throughput east-west microservices and latency-sensitive ingress traffic running on linux dataplane (`nftables`/`ipvs`) and cloud load balancers, delivering lowers cross-AZ data transfer costs (`trafficDistribution`) and reduces node CPU spent on iptables rules.
- **Workload-Aware & Gang Scheduling**: Improves workload-aware & gang scheduling for distributed ai training, multi-node batch jobs, ray/spark clusters, and mpi workloads running on high-density gpu/cpu batch pools and `kube-scheduler` queues, delivering prevents partial-allocation deadlocks where expensive GPU nodes sit idle waiting for peer workers.

## 2. Who Benefits? (Models, GPUs & Your Bill)
| Workload / Team | Models / Services | GPUs / Hardware | Practical Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Feature Enhancements** | General platform workloads and API consumers | Standard cluster nodes and runtime components | Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil |
| **Urgent Upgrade Notes Enhancements** | General platform workloads and API consumers | Standard cluster nodes and runtime components | Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil |
| **API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale** | Operator-heavy platforms, Argo CD / Flux GitOps controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ CRDs/Pods | Control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) CPU and memory footprint | Cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages |
| **Networking, `nftables` Proxy & Traffic Observability** | High-throughput east-west microservices and latency-sensitive ingress traffic | Linux dataplane (`nftables`/`ipvs`) and cloud load balancers | Lowers cross-AZ data transfer costs (`trafficDistribution`) and reduces node CPU spent on iptables rules |
| **Workload-Aware & Gang Scheduling (`PodGroup` / `Job` / Queueing)** | Distributed AI training, multi-node batch jobs, Ray/Spark clusters, and MPI workloads | High-density GPU/CPU batch pools and `kube-scheduler` queues | Prevents partial-allocation deadlocks where expensive GPU nodes sit idle waiting for peer workers |
| **CEL-Based Validating & Mutating Admission Policies** | Platform security guardrails, multi-tenant compliance policies, and default resource injectors | In-process `kube-apiserver` admission chain (replaces external webhook deployments) | Removes dedicated webhook pods and eliminates deployment outages caused by webhook timeouts |
| **Workload Identity, User Namespaces & Fine-Grained Authz** | Multi-tenant SaaS workloads, zero-trust service meshes, and privileged container migrations | Linux kernel namespaces, kubelet endpoints, and CSI secret injection paths | Reduces security agent/sidecar overhead and shrinks blast radius of container compromises |

## 3. What Does the Jargon Mean?
- **Gang Scheduling (`Workload` / `PodGroup`)**: An 'all-or-nothing' scheduling guarantee where a group of cooperating Pods (like a multi-node training or distributed inference job) only starts when capacity exists for the entire group. Why it matters: Prevents expensive GPUs from sitting idle in deadlocked partial allocations when a cluster is near capacity.
- **ValidatingAdmissionPolicy & MutatingAdmissionPolicy (CEL)**: In-process policy rules written in Common Expression Language (CEL) evaluated directly inside `kube-apiserver` without calling external admission webhook servers. Why it matters: Removes webhook network latency and prevents a crashed policy pod from taking down cluster deployments.
- **Linux User Namespaces (`hostUsers: false`)**: Maps the `root` user inside a container to an unprivileged non-root UID on the host node kernel. Why it matters: Dramatically reduces container-escape blast radius even for legacy workloads that require running as `root` inside the container.
- **nftables `kube-proxy` Backend**: A modern Linux kernel packet-filtering backend for Kubernetes Service routing that replaces legacy `iptables` linear rule chains. Why it matters: Cuts Service rule programming latency and CPU overhead on clusters with tens of thousands of Services.

## 4. Should I Upgrade?
**Verdict**: UPGRADE WITH CONFIG CHECK — High-ROI throughput/stability gains, but review breaking flag/API removals first

- **Technical change**: Creating a `Federated Ingress` is as simple as submitting an `Ingress` creation request to the Federation API Server. The Federation control system then creates and maintains a single global virtual.
- **Technical change**: Service loadBalancerSourceRanges doesn't respect updates ([#33033](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/33033)).
- **Technical change**: disallow user to update loadbalancerSourceRanges ([#33346](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/33346)).
- **Operational impact**: Lowers cross-AZ data transfer costs (`trafficDistribution`) and reduces node CPU spent on iptables rules
### 5. Workload-Aware & Gang Scheduling (`PodGroup` / `Job` / Queueing) (Upstream release notes)
- **Previously**: Prior to v1.4, teams operating workload-aware & gang scheduling relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on High-density GPU/CPU batch pools and `kube-scheduler` queues.
- **Technical change**: Introducing 'ScheduledJobs', which allow running time based Jobs, namely once at a specified time or repeatedly at specified point in time..
- **Technical change**: New resources and scheduler features (eg: `ScheduledJob` resource, pod/node affinity/anti-affinity).
- **Technical change**: kubectl rolling-update: < v1.4.0 client vs >=v1.4.0 cluster: Old version kubectl's rolling-update command is compatible with Kubernetes 1.4 and higher only if you specify a new replication controller.
- **Operational impact**: Prevents partial-allocation deadlocks where expensive GPU nodes sit idle waiting for peer workers
### 6. CEL-Based Validating & Mutating Admission Policies ([#31250](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/31250))
- **Previously**: Prior to v1.4, teams operating cel-based validating & mutating admission policies relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on In-process `kube-apiserver` admission chain (replaces external webhook deployments).
- **Technical change**: The NamespaceExists and NamespaceAutoProvision admission controllers have been removed, use the NamespaceLifecycle admission controller instead (#31250).
- **Technical change**: Container Image Policy allows an access controller to determine whether a pod may be scheduled based on a policy ([docs](http://kubernetes.io/docs/admin/admission-controllers/#imagepolicywebhook)).
- **Operational impact**: Removes dedicated webhook pods and eliminates deployment outages caused by webhook timeouts

high_level_changes.headline: API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves api server & etcd watch/cache efficiency at scale for operator-heavy platforms, argo cd / flux gitops controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ crds/pods running on control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) cpu and memory footprint, delivering cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages.

high_level_changes.headline: Dynamic Resource Allocation
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves dynamic resource allocation for ai/ml training, llm inference pods, fractional/multi-gpu workloads, and nic/fpga consumers running on nvidia/amd gpu nodes, multi-nic rdma clusters, and topology-aware hardware pools, delivering higher GPU utilization and fewer stranded accelerators via standardized device sharing and health reporting.

high_level_changes.headline: CEL-Based Validating & Mutating Admission Policies
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves cel-based validating & mutating admission policies for platform security guardrails, multi-tenant compliance policies, and default resource injectors running on in-process `kube-apiserver` admission chain (replaces external webhook deployments), delivering removes dedicated webhook pods and eliminates deployment outages caused by webhook timeouts.

high_level_changes.headline: Networking, `nftables` Proxy & Traffic Observability
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves networking, `nftables` proxy & traffic observability for high-throughput east-west microservices and latency-sensitive ingress traffic running on linux dataplane (`nftables`/`ipvs`) and cloud load balancers, delivering lowers cross-AZ data transfer costs (`trafficDistribution`) and reduces node CPU spent on iptables rules.

high_level_changes.headline: Feature Enhancements
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves feature enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.

jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Lets multiple pods share fractional GPUs safely or co-schedule across NVLink domains without custom vendor hacks.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Changing a running Pod's CPU or memory requests/limits dynamically without killing and recreating the container.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Eliminates cold-start restarts and dropped connections when scaling stateful services, databases, or warm AI model servers.

jargon_glossary.meaning: An 'all-or-nothing' scheduling guarantee where a group of cooperating Pods (like a multi-node training or distributed inference job) only starts when capacity exists for the entire group.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Prevents expensive GPUs from sitting idle in deadlocked partial allocations when a cluster is near capacity.

jargon_glossary.meaning: In-process policy rules written in Common Expression Language (CEL) evaluated directly inside `kube-apiserver` without calling external admission webhook servers.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Removes webhook network latency and prevents a crashed policy pod from taking down cluster deployments.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Streaming object lists from `kube-apiserver` memory cache snapshots instead of assembling giant one-shot payloads from `etcd`.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Slashes API server RAM spikes and protects `etcd` from OOM crashes during controller restarts on large clusters.

jargon_glossary.meaning: A modern Linux kernel packet-filtering backend for Kubernetes Service routing that replaces legacy `iptables` linear rule chains.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Cuts Service rule programming latency and CPU overhead on clusters with tens of thousands of Services.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Built-in kubelet provisioning and rotation of X.509 mTLS identity certificates directly into Pods without third-party sidecars.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Simplifies zero-trust pod-to-pod mTLS without managing complex external webhook/cert-manager plumbing.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Allows `HorizontalPodAutoscaler` to scale external/queue-driven workloads all the way down to 0 replicas when idle and wake them when queue depth rises.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Directly cuts cloud compute and GPU bills for bursty batch/inference workers during off-peak hours.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Concise Binary Object Representation (RFC 8949) as a compact binary alternative to JSON for Kubernetes API client-server serialization.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Reduces API server CPU spent on JSON parsing and lowers network bandwidth for custom resources (CRDs) that couldn't use Protobuf.

jargon_glossary.meaning: The standard plugin layer connecting Kubernetes PersistentVolumes to cloud block/file storage providers.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Controls how fast stateful workloads attach disks, recover from node failures, and handle credentials.

should_i_upgrade.text: ACTION REQUIRED: Graduated the `SELinuxMount` feature gate to GA. The feature is enabled by default in `v1.37`, which may break existing workloads in clusters with SELinux enabled. Please see [the Kubernetes blog post](https://kubernetes.io/blog/2026/04/22/breaking-changes-in-selinux-volume-labeling/) to identify potentially problematic workloads in a `v1.36` cluster and how to fix them or opt out of `SELinuxMount` changes before upgrading to `v1.37`. Admins of clusters without SELinux enabled can ignore this release note. ([#139956](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139956), [@jsafrane](https://github.com/jsafrane)) [SIG API Machinery, Apps and Node]

ACTION REQUIRED: Converted the `DisruptionMode` enum field to a struct to support future extensibility. Promoted the `scheduling.k8s.io` API group from `v1alpha2` to `v1alpha3` and dropped `v1alpha2` entirely. Remove all `v1alpha2` objects from the `kube-apiserver` before performing the cluster update. ([#138572](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/138572), [@dom4ha](https://github.com/dom4ha)) [SIG API Machinery, Apps, CLI, Etcd, Node, Scheduling and Testing]
sigs: API Machinery, Apps, CLI, Etcd, Node, Scheduling and Testing

should_i_upgrade.text: ACTION REQUIRED: Fixed `eventRecordQPS` handling in `kubelet` configuration to treat 0 as unlimited (no rate limit), aligning behavior with the documentation. Users relying on the previous default behavior should explicitly set a non-zero value (for example, 50). ([#117119](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/117119), [@HirazawaUi](https://github.com/HirazawaUi)) [SIG API Machinery, Auth and Node]

ACTION REQUIRED: Updated the `kubelet` to log its effective configuration at startup. Because these logs can expose configuration details, cluster administrators should restrict the `nodes/logs` ClusterRole to trusted users. This is largely a reminder of an existing best practice, since most effective configuration values can already be inferred from other log messages or `kubelet` behavior. ([#139837](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139837), [@SergeyKanzhelev](https://github.com/SergeyKanzhelev)) [SIG Node]

Changed `kubeadm` to explicitly set `KubeProxyConfiguration.mode` to iptables when `KubeProxyConfiguration` is not provided or when the `mode` field is empty. In `v1.37`, `kube-proxy` will warn if the field is not explicitly set as part of the planned transition to nftables as the default mode in a future release. ([#139777](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139777), [@neolit123](https://github.com/neolit123)) [SIG Cluster Lifecycle]
Deprecated the ignored `--filename`/`-f` flag on `kubectl run`. ([#138671](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/138671), [@Suknna](https://github.com/Suknna)) [SIG CLI]

Locked the deprecated `DeclarativeValidationTakeover` feature gate to its default value; it can no longer be set. ([#139212](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139212), [@yongruilin](https://github.com/yongruilin)) [SIG API Machinery]

`kubeadm`: Added a (delayed) warning that `kube-proxy`'s ipvs mode is deprecated since `v1.35` and users on newer Linux kernels should be using the nftables mode instead, which became GA in `v1.33`. For older kernel versions, users can use iptables, which is still the default. ([#139067](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139067), [@neolit123](https://github.com/neolit123)) [SIG Cluster Lifecycle]

([#140140](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/140140), [@p0lyn0mial](https://github.com/p0lyn0mial)) [SIG API Machinery]

Regular `Watch` requests are unaffected. ([#139308](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139308), [@p0lyn0mial](https://github.com/p0lyn0mial)) [SIG API Machinery]

Updated admission webhooks to skip auth/authz virtual resources, such as `tokenreviews` and `subjectaccessreviews`, that ValidatingAdmissionPolicy and MutatingAdmissionPolicy already exclude. Added the `ExcludeAdmissionWebhookVirtualResources` feature gate in Beta, enabled by default, with an opt-out option to restore the previous behavior. ([#140019](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/140019), [@BenTheElder](https://github.com/BenTheElder)) [SIG API Machinery and Testing]

([#139579](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139579), [@yt2985](https://github.com/yt2985)) [SIG API Machinery, Apps, Architecture, Auth, Etcd, Node, Scheduling and Testing]

# What's New in Kubernetes v1.37

## High-Level Explanation
Kubernetes v1.37 focuses on API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale, Dynamic Resource Allocation, and CEL-Based Validating & Mutating Admission Policies. For operators, this release translates 396 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

## 1. What Are the High-Level Changes?
- **API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale**: Improves api server & etcd watch/cache efficiency at scale for operator-heavy platforms, argo cd / flux gitops controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ crds/pods running on control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) cpu and memory footprint, delivering cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages.
- **Dynamic Resource Allocation**: Improves dynamic resource allocation for ai/ml training, llm inference pods, fractional/multi-gpu workloads, and nic/fpga consumers running on nvidia/amd gpu nodes, multi-nic rdma clusters, and topology-aware hardware pools, delivering higher GPU utilization and fewer stranded accelerators via standardized device sharing and health reporting.
- **CEL-Based Validating & Mutating Admission Policies**: Improves cel-based validating & mutating admission policies for platform security guardrails, multi-tenant compliance policies, and default resource injectors running on in-process `kube-apiserver` admission chain (replaces external webhook deployments), delivering removes dedicated webhook pods and eliminates deployment outages caused by webhook timeouts.
- **Networking, `nftables` Proxy & Traffic Observability**: Improves networking, `nftables` proxy & traffic observability for high-throughput east-west microservices and latency-sensitive ingress traffic running on linux dataplane (`nftables`/`ipvs`) and cloud load balancers, delivering lowers cross-AZ data transfer costs (`trafficDistribution`) and reduces node CPU spent on iptables rules.
- **Feature Enhancements**: Improves feature enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.

## 3. What Does the Jargon Mean?
- **DRA (Dynamic Resource Allocation)**: Kubernetes' next-generation API (`resource.k8s.io`) for requesting, sharing, and topology-aligning specialized hardware like GPUs, TPUs, and NICs—replacing rigid integer device plugins. Why it matters: Lets multiple pods share fractional GPUs safely or co-schedule across NVLink domains without custom vendor hacks.
- **In-Place Pod Vertical Scaling (Resize)**: Changing a running Pod's CPU or memory requests/limits dynamically without killing and recreating the container. Why it matters: Eliminates cold-start restarts and dropped connections when scaling stateful services, databases, or warm AI model servers.
- **Gang Scheduling (`Workload` / `PodGroup`)**: An 'all-or-nothing' scheduling guarantee where a group of cooperating Pods (like a multi-node training or distributed inference job) only starts when capacity exists for the entire group. Why it matters: Prevents expensive GPUs from sitting idle in deadlocked partial allocations when a cluster is near capacity.
- **ValidatingAdmissionPolicy & MutatingAdmissionPolicy (CEL)**: In-process policy rules written in Common Expression Language (CEL) evaluated directly inside `kube-apiserver` without calling external admission webhook servers. Why it matters: Removes webhook network latency and prevents a crashed policy pod from taking down cluster deployments.
- **WatchList & Snapshottable Watch Cache**: Streaming object lists from `kube-apiserver` memory cache snapshots instead of assembling giant one-shot payloads from `etcd`. Why it matters: Slashes API server RAM spikes and protects `etcd` from OOM crashes during controller restarts on large clusters.
- **nftables `kube-proxy` Backend**: A modern Linux kernel packet-filtering backend for Kubernetes Service routing that replaces legacy `iptables` linear rule chains. Why it matters: Cuts Service rule programming latency and CPU overhead on clusters with tens of thousands of Services.
- **Pod Certificates (`PodCertificateRequest`)**: Built-in kubelet provisioning and rotation of X.509 mTLS identity certificates directly into Pods without third-party sidecars. Why it matters: Simplifies zero-trust pod-to-pod mTLS without managing complex external webhook/cert-manager plumbing.
- **HPA Scale-to-Zero (`minReplicas: 0`)**: Allows `HorizontalPodAutoscaler` to scale external/queue-driven workloads all the way down to 0 replicas when idle and wake them when queue depth rises. Why it matters: Directly cuts cloud compute and GPU bills for bursty batch/inference workers during off-peak hours.
- **CBOR Encoding for Kubernetes API**: Concise Binary Object Representation (RFC 8949) as a compact binary alternative to JSON for Kubernetes API client-server serialization. Why it matters: Reduces API server CPU spent on JSON parsing and lowers network bandwidth for custom resources (CRDs) that couldn't use Protobuf.
- **CSI (Container Storage Interface)**: The standard plugin layer connecting Kubernetes PersistentVolumes to cloud block/file storage providers. Why it matters: Controls how fast stateful workloads attach disks, recover from node failures, and handle credentials.

kubernetes_guides.positioning: Kubernetes v1.36 focuses on Dynamic Resource Allocation, Feature Enhancements, and API Change Enhancements. For operators, this release translates 347 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

high_level_changes.headline: Dynamic Resource Allocation
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves dynamic resource allocation for ai/ml training, llm inference pods, fractional/multi-gpu workloads, and nic/fpga consumers running on nvidia/amd gpu nodes, multi-nic rdma clusters, and topology-aware hardware pools, delivering higher GPU utilization and fewer stranded accelerators via standardized device sharing and health reporting.

high_level_changes.headline: Feature Enhancements
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves feature enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.

high_level_changes.headline: API Change Enhancements
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves api change enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.

high_level_changes.headline: Workload-Aware & Gang Scheduling
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves workload-aware & gang scheduling for distributed ai training, multi-node batch jobs, ray/spark clusters, and mpi workloads running on high-density gpu/cpu batch pools and `kube-scheduler` queues, delivering prevents partial-allocation deadlocks where expensive GPU nodes sit idle waiting for peer workers.

high_level_changes.headline: API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves api server & etcd watch/cache efficiency at scale for operator-heavy platforms, argo cd / flux gitops controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ crds/pods running on control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) cpu and memory footprint, delivering cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Kubernetes' next-generation API (`resource.k8s.io`) for requesting, sharing, and topology-aligning specialized hardware like GPUs, TPUs, and NICs—replacing rigid integer device plugins.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Lets multiple pods share fractional GPUs safely or co-schedule across NVLink domains without custom vendor hacks.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Changing a running Pod's CPU or memory requests/limits dynamically without killing and recreating the container.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Eliminates cold-start restarts and dropped connections when scaling stateful services, databases, or warm AI model servers.

jargon_glossary.meaning: An 'all-or-nothing' scheduling guarantee where a group of cooperating Pods (like a multi-node training or distributed inference job) only starts when capacity exists for the entire group.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Prevents expensive GPUs from sitting idle in deadlocked partial allocations when a cluster is near capacity.

jargon_glossary.meaning: First-class lifecycle support for helper containers (log shippers, service mesh proxies) so they start before the main app and terminate automatically after Batch Jobs finish.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Fixes the classic Kubernetes bug where a finished Job hangs forever because an Istio/Envoy sidecar stays alive.

jargon_glossary.meaning: In-process policy rules written in Common Expression Language (CEL) evaluated directly inside `kube-apiserver` without calling external admission webhook servers.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Removes webhook network latency and prevents a crashed policy pod from taking down cluster deployments.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Maps the `root` user inside a container to an unprivileged non-root UID on the host node kernel.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Dramatically reduces container-escape blast radius even for legacy workloads that require running as `root` inside the container.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Streaming object lists from `kube-apiserver` memory cache snapshots instead of assembling giant one-shot payloads from `etcd`.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Slashes API server RAM spikes and protects `etcd` from OOM crashes during controller restarts on large clusters.

jargon_glossary.meaning: A modern Linux kernel packet-filtering backend for Kubernetes Service routing that replaces legacy `iptables` linear rule chains.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Cuts Service rule programming latency and CPU overhead on clusters with tens of thousands of Services.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Allows `HorizontalPodAutoscaler` to scale external/queue-driven workloads all the way down to 0 replicas when idle and wake them when queue depth rises.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Directly cuts cloud compute and GPU bills for bursty batch/inference workers during off-peak hours.

jargon_glossary.meaning: The standard plugin layer connecting Kubernetes PersistentVolumes to cloud block/file storage providers.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Controls how fast stateful workloads attach disks, recover from node failures, and handle credentials.

should_i_upgrade.text: ACTION REQUIRED: kube-controller-manager: Renamed metric `volume_operation_total_errors` to `volume_operation_errors_total`. If you are using custom monitoring dashboards or alerting rules based on the `volume_operation_total_errors` metric, update them to use the new `volume_operation_errors_total` metric. ([#136399](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/136399), [@tico88612](https://github.com/tico88612)) [SIG Apps, Instrumentation, Storage and Testing]

Added support for running PreBind plugins in parallel in the scheduler framework to improve binding latency. ACTION REQUIRED: Plugins can opt-in to parallel execution by returning `AllowParallel: true` from the `PreBindPreFlight` method. PreBind plugin implementations need to be updated to return `PreBindPreFlightResult` from the `PreBindPreFlight` method; returning nil retains the existing sequential behavior. ([#135393](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/135393), [@tosi3k](https://github.com/tosi3k)) [SIG Node, Scheduling, Storage and Testing]

Added warnings and deprecation for Service `.spec.externalIPs`. ([#137293](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137293), [@adrianmoisey](https://github.com/adrianmoisey)) [SIG Apps, Network and Windows]

Direct access to the `Raw` field of `metav1.FieldsV1` is deprecated. Code that constructs or reads `FieldsV1` should migrate to the new `NewFieldsV1(string)`, `GetRawBytes()`, `GetRawString()`, and `SetRawBytes()` accessor methods. ([#137304](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137304), [@aaron-prindle](https://github.com/aaron-prindle)) [SIG API Machinery, Apps and Testing]

Disabled `git-repo` volume plugin by default, with no option to turn it back on. ([#136400](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/136400), [@vinayakankugoyal](https://github.com/vinayakankugoyal)) [SIG Storage]

Renamed `AllowlistEntry.Name` to `AllowlistEntry.Command` in the credential plugin allowlist. ([#137272](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137272), [@pmengelbert](https://github.com/pmengelbert)) [SIG API Machinery, Auth, CLI and Testing]
sigs: API Machinery, Auth, CLI and Testing

should_i_upgrade.text: DRA ResourceSlice controller: Added optional `ReconcilePoolWithName` to allow per-pool reconciliation without setting `NodeName` on slices, so the scheduler can use `NodeSelector` or `allNodes` for node-owned, cluster-visible resources (e.g. network-shared devices). "All nodes" is no longer the default. When publishing devices for the entire cluster, it must be set explicitly. ([#137365](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137365), [@yaroslavborbat](https://github.com/yaroslavborbat)) [SIG Node and Testing]

Removed the in-tree Portworx volume plugin, completing the migration to CSI. Removed the GA `CSIMigrationPortworx` feature gate (locked since `v1.33`) and alpha `InTreePluginPortworxUnregister` feature gate, with all operations now redirected to CSI. ([#135322](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/135322), [@carlory](https://github.com/carlory)) [SIG API Machinery, Apps, Auth, Node, Scalability, Scheduling, Storage and Testing]
sigs: API Machinery, Apps, Auth, Node, Scalability, Scheduling, Storage and Testing

should_i_upgrade.text: Client-go: Default informer behavior now updates store state with all the objects in a list or relist before calling handler `OnDelete`, `OnAdd`, or `OnUpdate` methods for individual items which were deleted, added, or removed. This ensures that the store state which can be inspected by handlers corresponds to a set of objects that existed at a particular resource version on the server. This behavior is guarded by the `AtomicFIFO` feature gate, which is enabled by default in `v1.36` but can be disabled if needed to temporarily regain the previous behavior. ([#135462](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/135462), [@michaelasp](https://github.com/michaelasp)) [SIG API Machinery]

ACTION REQUIRED: DRA (Dynamic Resource Allocation) drivers and controllers now require granular RBAC permissions to update ResourceClaim statuses when the `DRAResourceClaimGranularStatusAuthorization` feature gate is enabled (beta in `v1.36`). Schedulers and controllers must be granted `update`/`patch` on `resourceclaims/binding`. DRA drivers must be granted `associated-node:update` or `arbitrary-node:update` (or patch equivalents) on `resourceclaims/driver`, restricted by their specific `resourceNames`. ([#134947](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/134947), [@aojea](https://github.com/aojea)) [SIG API Machinery, Apps, Auth, Instrumentation, Node, Scheduling and Testing]
sigs: API Machinery, Apps, Auth, Instrumentation, Node, Scheduling and Testing

technical_deep_dive.theme: Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) & GPU/Accelerator Management
technical_deep_dive.previously: Prior to v1.36, teams operating dynamic resource allocation relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on NVIDIA/AMD GPU nodes, multi-NIC RDMA clusters, and topology-aware hardware pools.
tech_bullets: DRA: Graduated Device Binding Conditions (KEP #5007) to beta, enabled by default in `v1.36`. ([#137795](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137795).

# What's New in Kubernetes v1.36

## High-Level Explanation
Kubernetes v1.36 focuses on Dynamic Resource Allocation, Feature Enhancements, and API Change Enhancements. For operators, this release translates 347 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

## 1. What Are the High-Level Changes?
- **Dynamic Resource Allocation**: Improves dynamic resource allocation for ai/ml training, llm inference pods, fractional/multi-gpu workloads, and nic/fpga consumers running on nvidia/amd gpu nodes, multi-nic rdma clusters, and topology-aware hardware pools, delivering higher GPU utilization and fewer stranded accelerators via standardized device sharing and health reporting.
- **Feature Enhancements**: Improves feature enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.
- **API Change Enhancements**: Improves api change enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.
- **Workload-Aware & Gang Scheduling**: Improves workload-aware & gang scheduling for distributed ai training, multi-node batch jobs, ray/spark clusters, and mpi workloads running on high-density gpu/cpu batch pools and `kube-scheduler` queues, delivering prevents partial-allocation deadlocks where expensive GPU nodes sit idle waiting for peer workers.
- **API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale**: Improves api server & etcd watch/cache efficiency at scale for operator-heavy platforms, argo cd / flux gitops controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ crds/pods running on control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) cpu and memory footprint, delivering cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages.

## 2. Who Benefits? (Models, GPUs & Your Bill)
| Workload / Team | Models / Services | GPUs / Hardware | Practical Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) & GPU/Accelerator Management** | AI/ML training, LLM inference pods, fractional/multi-GPU workloads, and NIC/FPGA consumers | NVIDIA/AMD GPU nodes, multi-NIC RDMA clusters, and topology-aware hardware pools | Higher GPU utilization and fewer stranded accelerators via standardized device sharing and health reporting |
| **Feature Enhancements** | General platform workloads and API consumers | Standard cluster nodes and runtime components | Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil |
| **API Change Enhancements** | General platform workloads and API consumers | Standard cluster nodes and runtime components | Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil |
| **Workload-Aware & Gang Scheduling (`PodGroup` / `Job` / Queueing)** | Distributed AI training, multi-node batch jobs, Ray/Spark clusters, and MPI workloads | High-density GPU/CPU batch pools and `kube-scheduler` queues | Prevents partial-allocation deadlocks where expensive GPU nodes sit idle waiting for peer workers |
| **API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale** | Operator-heavy platforms, Argo CD / Flux GitOps controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ CRDs/Pods | Control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) CPU and memory footprint | Cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages |
| **CEL-Based Validating & Mutating Admission Policies** | Platform security guardrails, multi-tenant compliance policies, and default resource injectors | In-process `kube-apiserver` admission chain (replaces external webhook deployments) | Removes dedicated webhook pods and eliminates deployment outages caused by webhook timeouts |
| **In-Place Pod Vertical Scaling (Zero-Restart Resource Resize)** | Stateful microservices, warm inference engines, JVMs, and suspended Batch Jobs needing CPU/RAM adjustments | Linux worker nodes and kubelet resource allocation loops | Eliminates over-provisioning buffer and avoids expensive pod restart cold-starts during traffic spikes |

## 3. What Does the Jargon Mean?
- **DRA (Dynamic Resource Allocation)**: Kubernetes' next-generation API (`resource.k8s.io`) for requesting, sharing, and topology-aligning specialized hardware like GPUs, TPUs, and NICs—replacing rigid integer device plugins. Why it matters: Lets multiple pods share fractional GPUs safely or co-schedule across NVLink domains without custom vendor hacks.
- **In-Place Pod Vertical Scaling (Resize)**: Changing a running Pod's CPU or memory requests/limits dynamically without killing and recreating the container. Why it matters: Eliminates cold-start restarts and dropped connections when scaling stateful services, databases, or warm AI model servers.
- **Gang Scheduling (`Workload` / `PodGroup`)**: An 'all-or-nothing' scheduling guarantee where a group of cooperating Pods (like a multi-node training or distributed inference job) only starts when capacity exists for the entire group. Why it matters: Prevents expensive GPUs from sitting idle in deadlocked partial allocations when a cluster is near capacity.
- **Native Sidecar Containers (`initContainers` with `restartPolicy: Always`)**: First-class lifecycle support for helper containers (log shippers, service mesh proxies) so they start before the main app and terminate automatically after Batch Jobs finish. Why it matters: Fixes the classic Kubernetes bug where a finished Job hangs forever because an Istio/Envoy sidecar stays alive.
- **ValidatingAdmissionPolicy & MutatingAdmissionPolicy (CEL)**: In-process policy rules written in Common Expression Language (CEL) evaluated directly inside `kube-apiserver` without calling external admission webhook servers. Why it matters: Removes webhook network latency and prevents a crashed policy pod from taking down cluster deployments.
- **Linux User Namespaces (`hostUsers: false`)**: Maps the `root` user inside a container to an unprivileged non-root UID on the host node kernel. Why it matters: Dramatically reduces container-escape blast radius even for legacy workloads that require running as `root` inside the container.
- **WatchList & Snapshottable Watch Cache**: Streaming object lists from `kube-apiserver` memory cache snapshots instead of assembling giant one-shot payloads from `etcd`. Why it matters: Slashes API server RAM spikes and protects `etcd` from OOM crashes during controller restarts on large clusters.
- **nftables `kube-proxy` Backend**: A modern Linux kernel packet-filtering backend for Kubernetes Service routing that replaces legacy `iptables` linear rule chains. Why it matters: Cuts Service rule programming latency and CPU overhead on clusters with tens of thousands of Services.
- **HPA Scale-to-Zero (`minReplicas: 0`)**: Allows `HorizontalPodAutoscaler` to scale external/queue-driven workloads all the way down to 0 replicas when idle and wake them when queue depth rises. Why it matters: Directly cuts cloud compute and GPU bills for bursty batch/inference workers during off-peak hours.
- **CSI (Container Storage Interface)**: The standard plugin layer connecting Kubernetes PersistentVolumes to cloud block/file storage providers. Why it matters: Controls how fast stateful workloads attach disks, recover from node failures, and handle credentials.

## 4. Should I Upgrade?
**Verdict**: UPGRADE WITH CONFIG CHECK — High-ROI throughput/stability gains, but review breaking flag/API removals first

- **Urgent Upgrade Notes**: Added support for running PreBind plugins in parallel in the scheduler framework to improve binding latency. high_level_changes.headline: API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves api server & etcd watch/cache efficiency at scale for operator-heavy platforms, argo cd / flux gitops controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ crds/pods running on control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) cpu and memory footprint, delivering cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages.

high_level_changes.headline: Dynamic Resource Allocation
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves dynamic resource allocation for ai/ml training, llm inference pods, fractional/multi-gpu workloads, and nic/fpga consumers running on nvidia/amd gpu nodes, multi-nic rdma clusters, and topology-aware hardware pools, delivering higher GPU utilization and fewer stranded accelerators via standardized device sharing and health reporting.

high_level_changes.headline: Feature Enhancements
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves feature enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.

high_level_changes.headline: Workload-Aware & Gang Scheduling
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves workload-aware & gang scheduling for distributed ai training, multi-node batch jobs, ray/spark clusters, and mpi workloads running on high-density gpu/cpu batch pools and `kube-scheduler` queues, delivering prevents partial-allocation deadlocks where expensive GPU nodes sit idle waiting for peer workers.

high_level_changes.headline: API Change Enhancements
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves api change enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Kubernetes' next-generation API (`resource.k8s.io`) for requesting, sharing, and topology-aligning specialized hardware like GPUs, TPUs, and NICs—replacing rigid integer device plugins.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Lets multiple pods share fractional GPUs safely or co-schedule across NVLink domains without custom vendor hacks.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Changing a running Pod's CPU or memory requests/limits dynamically without killing and recreating the container.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Eliminates cold-start restarts and dropped connections when scaling stateful services, databases, or warm AI model servers.

jargon_glossary.meaning: An 'all-or-nothing' scheduling guarantee where a group of cooperating Pods (like a multi-node training or distributed inference job) only starts when capacity exists for the entire group.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Prevents expensive GPUs from sitting idle in deadlocked partial allocations when a cluster is near capacity.

jargon_glossary.meaning: First-class lifecycle support for helper containers (log shippers, service mesh proxies) so they start before the main app and terminate automatically after Batch Jobs finish.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Fixes the classic Kubernetes bug where a finished Job hangs forever because an Istio/Envoy sidecar stays alive.

jargon_glossary.meaning: In-process policy rules written in Common Expression Language (CEL) evaluated directly inside `kube-apiserver` without calling external admission webhook servers.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Removes webhook network latency and prevents a crashed policy pod from taking down cluster deployments.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Maps the `root` user inside a container to an unprivileged non-root UID on the host node kernel.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Dramatically reduces container-escape blast radius even for legacy workloads that require running as `root` inside the container.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Streaming object lists from `kube-apiserver` memory cache snapshots instead of assembling giant one-shot payloads from `etcd`.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Slashes API server RAM spikes and protects `etcd` from OOM crashes during controller restarts on large clusters.

jargon_glossary.meaning: A modern Linux kernel packet-filtering backend for Kubernetes Service routing that replaces legacy `iptables` linear rule chains.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Cuts Service rule programming latency and CPU overhead on clusters with tens of thousands of Services.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Built-in kubelet provisioning and rotation of X.509 mTLS identity certificates directly into Pods without third-party sidecars.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Simplifies zero-trust pod-to-pod mTLS without managing complex external webhook/cert-manager plumbing.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Allows `HorizontalPodAutoscaler` to scale external/queue-driven workloads all the way down to 0 replicas when idle and wake them when queue depth rises.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Directly cuts cloud compute and GPU bills for bursty batch/inference workers during off-peak hours.

jargon_glossary.meaning: The standard plugin layer connecting Kubernetes PersistentVolumes to cloud block/file storage providers.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Controls how fast stateful workloads attach disks, recover from node failures, and handle credentials.

should_i_upgrade.text: ACTION REQUIRED: Removed the `--pod-infra-container-image` flag from `kubelet` command line. For `non-kubeadm` clusters, users must manually remove this flag from their `kubelet` configuration to prevent startup failures before upgrading `kubelet`. For `kubeadm` clusters, if users pass extra arguments to the `kubelet` like `--pod-infra-container-image`, it will be written to the `kubelet` env file during the `init` phase. `kubeadm` does not remove it during the `init` or `join` phase, so users must manually remove it from `extraArgs` in the `kubelet` configuration file. ([#133779](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/133779), [@carlory](https://github.com/carlory))

ACTION REQUIRED: vendor: Updated `k8s.io/system-validators` to `v1.12.1`. The cgroups validator now throws an error instead of a warning if cgroups v1 is detected on the host and the provided KubeletVersion is `v1.35` or newer. kubeadm: Started using `k8s.io/system-validators` `v1.12.1` in `kubeadm` `v1.35`. During `kubeadm init`, `kubeadm join`, and `kubeadm upgrade`, the SystemVerification preflight check throws an error if cgroups v1 is detected and the detected `kubelet` version is `v1.35` or newer. For older versions of `kubelet`, a preflight warning is displayed. To allow cgroups v1 with `kubeadm` and `kubelet` version `v1.35` or newer, you must:
Ignore the error from the SystemVerification preflight check by `kubeadm`.

Edit the `kube-system/kubelet-config` ConfigMap and add the `failCgroupV1: false` field before upgrading. ([#134744](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/134744), [@neolit123](https://github.com/neolit123)) [SIG Cluster Lifecycle and Node]

ACTION REQUIRED: `failCgroupV1` will be set to true from 1.35. This means that nodes will not start on a cgroup v1 by default. This puts cgroup v1 into a deprecated state. ([#134298](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/134298), [@kannon92](https://github.com/kannon92))

Marked `ipvs` mode in kube-proxy as deprecated, which will be removed in a future version of Kubernetes. Users are encouraged to migrate to `nftables`. ([#134539](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/134539), [@adrianmoisey](https://github.com/adrianmoisey))

Kubeadm: Graduated the kubeadm-specific feature gate `ControlPlaneKubeletLocalMode` to GA and locked it to enabled by default. To opt out, patch the `server` field in `/etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf`. Deprecated the subphase of `kubeadm join phase control-plane-join` called `etcd`, which is now hidden and replaced by subphase with identical functionality `etcd-join`. The `etcd` subphase will be removed in a future release. The subphase `kubelet-wait-bootstrap` of `kubeadm join` is no longer experimental and will now always run. ([#134106](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/134106), [@neolit123](https://github.com/neolit123))

Promoted the `JobManagedBy` feature to general availability. The `JobManagedBy` feature gate was locked to `true` and will be removed in a future Kubernetes release. ([#135080](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/135080), [@dejanzele](https://github.com/dejanzele)) [SIG API Machinery, Apps and Testing]

Promoted the `EnvFiles` feature gate to beta and is enabled by default. Additionally, the syntax specification for environment variables has been restricted to a subset of POSIX shell syntax (all variable values must be wrapped in single quotes). ([#134414](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/134414), [@HirazawaUi](https://github.com/HirazawaUi)) [SIG Node and Testing]

The `PreferSameZone` and `PreferSameNode` values for the Service `trafficDistribution` field graduated to general availability. The `PreferClose` value is now deprecated in favor of the more explicit `PreferSameZone`. ([#134457](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/134457), [@danwinship](https://github.com/danwinship)) [SIG API Machinery, Apps, Network and Testing]
sigs: API Machinery, Apps, Network and Testing

tech_bullets: Kubeadm: Graduated the kubeadm-specific feature gate `ControlPlaneKubeletLocalMode` to GA and locked it to enabled by default. To opt out, patch the `server` field in `/etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf`. (#134106).

Kube-apiserver: Made the subresources `pods/exec`, `pods/attach`, and `pods/portforward` require `create` permission for both SPDY and Websocket API requests. Previously, SPDY requests required (#134577).

The Pod Certificates feature moved to beta. The `PodCertificateRequest` feature gate is set disabled by default. To use the feature, users must enable the certificates API groups in `v1beta1` and (#134624).

Added the `StorageVersionMigration` `v1beta1` API and removed the `v1alpha1` API. ACTION REQUIRED: The `v1alpha1` API is no longer supported. Users must remove any `v1alpha1` resources before (#134784).
technical_deep_dive.why_it_matters: Cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages

tech_bullets: DRA: The `DynamicResourceAllocation` feature gate for the core functionality (GA in `v1.34`) has now been locked to enabled-by-default and cannot be disabled anymore. (#134452).

The `PreferSameZone` and `PreferSameNode` values for the Service `trafficDistribution` field graduated to general availability. The `PreferClose` value is now deprecated in favor of the more explicit (#134457).

The DRA device taints and toleration feature received a separate feature gate, `DRADeviceTaintRules`, which controlled support for `DeviceTaintRules`. This allowed disabling it while keeping (#135068).
Documentation: - Promoted the `--chunk-size` flag to stable. The kubectl `describe`, `get`, `drain`, and `events` commands can use `--chunk-size` flag to set chunk size. (#134481).
technical_deep_dive.why_it_matters: Higher GPU utilization and fewer stranded accelerators via standardized device sharing and health reporting
