wheres_the_proof.text: SIG API Machinery: This release SIG API Machinery focused mainly on CustomResources. For example, subresources for CustomResources are now beta and enabled by default. With this, updates to the `/status` subresource will disallow updates to all fields other than `.status` (not just `.spec` and `.metadata` as before). Also, `required` and `description` can be used at the root of the CRD OpenAPI validation schema when the `/status` subresource is enabled. In addition, users can now create multiple versions of CustomResourceDefinitions, but without any kind of automatic conversion, and CustomResourceDefinitions now allow specification of additional columns for `kubectl get` output via the `spec.additionalPrinterColumns` field.

Graduated to Beta: * The Sysctls experimental feature has been promoted to beta (enabled by default via the `Sysctls` feature flag). PodSecurityPolicy and Pod objects now have fields for specifying and controlling sysctls. Alpha sysctl annotations will be ignored by 1.11+ kubelets. All alpha sysctl annotations in existing deployments must be converted to API fields to be effective. ([#6371](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/63717), [@ingvagabund](https://github.com/ingvagabund))

Graduated to Beta: * Subresources for custom resources is now considered beta and enabled by default. With this, updates to the `/status` subresource will disallow updates to all fields other than `.status` (not just `.spec` and `.metadata` as before). Also, `required` can be used at the root of the CRD OpenAPI validation schema when the `/status` subresource is enabled. ([#63598](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/63598), [@nikhita](https://github.com/nikhita))

Graduated to Beta: * The `PriorityClass` API has been promoted to `scheduling.k8s.io/v1beta1` ([#63100](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/63100), [@ravisantoshgudimetla](https://github.com/ravisantoshgudimetla))

Graduated to Beta: * The dynamic Kubelet config feature is now beta, and the DynamicKubeletConfig feature gate is on by default. In order to use dynamic Kubelet config, ensure that the Kubelet's --dynamic-config-dir option is set.  ([#64275](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/64275), [@mtaufen](https://github.com/mtaufen))
Graduated to Beta: * Volume expansion is now considered Beta. ([#64288](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/64288), [@gnufied](https://github.com/gnufied))

Graduated to Beta: * CRI container log rotation is now considered beta, and is enabled by default. ([#64046](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/64046), [@yujuhong](https://github.com/yujuhong))

Graduated to Beta: * client-go: credential exec plugins is now considered beta. ([#64482](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/64482), [@ericchiang](https://github.com/ericchiang))

SIG Auth: Work this cycle focused on graduating existing functions, and on making security functions more understandable for users. RBAC [cluster role aggregation](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/rbac/#aggregated-clusterroles), introduced in 1.9, graduated to stable status with no changes in 1.11, and [client-go credential plugins](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/authentication/#client-go-credential-plugins)  graduated to beta status, while also adding support for obtaining TLS credentials from an external plugin. Kubernetes 1.11 also makes it easier to see what's happening, as audit events can now be annotated with information about how an API request was handled:

SIG Node: SIG-Node advanced several features and made incremental improvements in a few key topic areas this release. The dynamic kubelet config feature graduated to beta, so it is enabled by default, simplifying management of the node object itself.  Kubelets that are configured to work with the CRI may take advantage of the log rotation feature, which is graduating to beta this release. The cri-tools project, which aims to provide consistent tooling for operators to debug and introspect their nodes in production independent of their chosen container runtime, graduated to GA. As far as platforms, working with SIG-Windows, enhancements were made to the kubelet to improve platform support on Windows operating systems, and improvements to resource management were also made.  In particular, support for sysctls on Linux graduated to beta.

Note that this involves [significant and important changes for operators](https://github.com/kubernetes/sig-release/pull/201/files). The team also worked on improved performance and reliability of the scheduler.

# What's New in Kubernetes v1.11

## High-Level Explanation
Kubernetes v1.11 focuses on Feature Enhancements, API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale, and StatefulSet PVC Auto-Cleanup, Volume Health & Storage Expansion. For operators, this release translates 436 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

## 1. What Are the High-Level Changes?
- **Feature Enhancements**: Improves feature enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.
- **API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale**: Improves api server & etcd watch/cache efficiency at scale for operator-heavy platforms, argo cd / flux gitops controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ crds/pods running on control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) cpu and memory footprint, delivering cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages.
- **StatefulSet PVC Auto-Cleanup, Volume Health & Storage Expansion**: Improves statefulset pvc auto-cleanup, volume health & storage expansion for databases, kafka/clickhouse clusters, and stateful ai checkpoint storage running on csi storage drivers and cloud block volumes, delivering eliminates orphaned cloud disk charges when scaling down or deleting temporary StatefulSets.
- **CEL-Based Validating & Mutating Admission Policies**: Improves cel-based validating & mutating admission policies for platform security guardrails, multi-tenant compliance policies, and default resource injectors running on in-process `kube-apiserver` admission chain (replaces external webhook deployments), delivering removes dedicated webhook pods and eliminates deployment outages caused by webhook timeouts.
- **Networking, `nftables` Proxy & Traffic Observability**: Improves networking, `nftables` proxy & traffic observability for high-throughput east-west microservices and latency-sensitive ingress traffic running on linux dataplane (`nftables`/`ipvs`) and cloud load balancers, delivering lowers cross-AZ data transfer costs (`trafficDistribution`) and reduces node CPU spent on iptables rules.

## 2. Who Benefits? (Models, GPUs & Your Bill)
| Workload / Team | Models / Services | GPUs / Hardware | Practical Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Feature Enhancements** | General platform workloads and API consumers | Standard cluster nodes and runtime components | Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil |
| **API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale** | Operator-heavy platforms, Argo CD / Flux GitOps controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ CRDs/Pods | Control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) CPU and memory footprint | Cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages |
| **StatefulSet PVC Auto-Cleanup, Volume Health & Storage Expansion** | Databases, Kafka/ClickHouse clusters, and stateful AI checkpoint storage | CSI storage drivers and cloud block volumes | Eliminates orphaned cloud disk charges when scaling down or deleting temporary StatefulSets |
| **CEL-Based Validating & Mutating Admission Policies** | Platform security guardrails, multi-tenant compliance policies, and default resource injectors | In-process `kube-apiserver` admission chain (replaces external webhook deployments) | Removes dedicated webhook pods and eliminates deployment outages caused by webhook timeouts |
| **Networking, `nftables` Proxy & Traffic Observability** | High-throughput east-west microservices and latency-sensitive ingress traffic | Linux dataplane (`nftables`/`ipvs`) and cloud load balancers | Lowers cross-AZ data transfer costs (`trafficDistribution`) and reduces node CPU spent on iptables rules |
| **Urgent Upgrade Notes Enhancements** | General platform workloads and API consumers | Standard cluster nodes and runtime components | Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil |
| **Workload-Aware & Gang Scheduling (`PodGroup` / `Job` / Queueing)** | Distributed AI training, multi-node batch jobs, Ray/Spark clusters, and MPI workloads | High-density GPU/CPU batch pools and `kube-scheduler` queues | Prevents partial-allocation deadlocks where expensive GPU nodes sit idle waiting for peer workers |

## 3. What Does the Jargon Mean?
- **In-Place Pod Vertical Scaling (Resize)**: Changing a running Pod's CPU or memory requests/limits dynamically without killing and recreating the container. Why it matters: Eliminates cold-start restarts and dropped connections when scaling stateful services, databases, or warm AI model servers.
- **Gang Scheduling (`Workload` / `PodGroup`)**: An 'all-or-nothing' scheduling guarantee where a group of cooperating Pods (like a multi-node training or distributed inference job) only starts when capacity exists for the entire group. Why it matters: Prevents expensive GPUs from sitting idle in deadlocked partial allocations when a cluster is near capacity.
- **ValidatingAdmissionPolicy & MutatingAdmissionPolicy (CEL)**: In-process policy rules written in Common Expression Language (CEL) evaluated directly inside `kube-apiserver` without calling external admission webhook servers. Why it matters: Removes webhook network latency and prevents a crashed policy pod from taking down cluster deployments.
- **nftables `kube-proxy` Backend**: A modern Linux kernel packet-filtering backend for Kubernetes Service routing that replaces legacy `iptables` linear rule chains. Why it matters: Cuts Service rule programming latency and CPU overhead on clusters with tens of thousands of Services.
- **CSI (Container Storage Interface)**: The standard plugin layer connecting Kubernetes PersistentVolumes to cloud block/file storage providers. Why it matters: Controls how fast stateful workloads attach disks, recover from node failures, and handle credentials.

kubernetes_guides.positioning: Kubernetes v1.10 focuses on Feature Enhancements, StatefulSet PVC Auto-Cleanup, Volume Health & Storage Expansion, and Dynamic Resource Allocation. For operators, this release translates 435 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.
kubernetes_guides.high_level_explanation: Kubernetes v1.10 focuses on Feature Enhancements, StatefulSet PVC Auto-Cleanup, Volume Health & Storage Expansion, and Dynamic Resource Allocation. For operators, this release translates 435 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.
kubernetes_guides.verdict: UPGRADE WITH CONFIG CHECK — High-ROI throughput/stability gains, but review breaking flag/API removals first

high_level_changes.headline: Feature Enhancements
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves feature enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.

high_level_changes.headline: StatefulSet PVC Auto-Cleanup, Volume Health & Storage Expansion
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves statefulset pvc auto-cleanup, volume health & storage expansion for databases, kafka/clickhouse clusters, and stateful ai checkpoint storage running on csi storage drivers and cloud block volumes, delivering eliminates orphaned cloud disk charges when scaling down or deleting temporary StatefulSets.

high_level_changes.headline: Dynamic Resource Allocation
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves dynamic resource allocation for ai/ml training, llm inference pods, fractional/multi-gpu workloads, and nic/fpga consumers running on nvidia/amd gpu nodes, multi-nic rdma clusters, and topology-aware hardware pools, delivering higher GPU utilization and fewer stranded accelerators via standardized device sharing and health reporting.

high_level_changes.headline: API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves api server & etcd watch/cache efficiency at scale for operator-heavy platforms, argo cd / flux gitops controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ crds/pods running on control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) cpu and memory footprint, delivering cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages.

high_level_changes.headline: Deprecation Enhancements
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves deprecation enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Kubernetes' next-generation API (`resource.k8s.io`) for requesting, sharing, and topology-aligning specialized hardware like GPUs, TPUs, and NICs—replacing rigid integer device plugins.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Lets multiple pods share fractional GPUs safely or co-schedule across NVLink domains without custom vendor hacks.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Changing a running Pod's CPU or memory requests/limits dynamically without killing and recreating the container.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Eliminates cold-start restarts and dropped connections when scaling stateful services, databases, or warm AI model servers.

jargon_glossary.meaning: First-class lifecycle support for helper containers (log shippers, service mesh proxies) so they start before the main app and terminate automatically after Batch Jobs finish.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Fixes the classic Kubernetes bug where a finished Job hangs forever because an Istio/Envoy sidecar stays alive.

jargon_glossary.meaning: In-process policy rules written in Common Expression Language (CEL) evaluated directly inside `kube-apiserver` without calling external admission webhook servers.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Removes webhook network latency and prevents a crashed policy pod from taking down cluster deployments.

jargon_glossary.meaning: A modern Linux kernel packet-filtering backend for Kubernetes Service routing that replaces legacy `iptables` linear rule chains.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Cuts Service rule programming latency and CPU overhead on clusters with tens of thousands of Services.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Allows `HorizontalPodAutoscaler` to scale external/queue-driven workloads all the way down to 0 replicas when idle and wake them when queue depth rises.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Directly cuts cloud compute and GPU bills for bursty batch/inference workers during off-peak hours.

jargon_glossary.meaning: The standard plugin layer connecting Kubernetes PersistentVolumes to cloud block/file storage providers.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Controls how fast stateful workloads attach disks, recover from node failures, and handle credentials.

should_i_upgrade.text: If you need to downgrade from 1.10 to 1.9.x, downgrade to v1.9.6 to ensure PV and PVC objects can be deleted properly.

Use of subPath module with hostPath volumes can cause issues during reconstruction ([#61446](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/61446)) and with containerized kubelets ([#61456](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/61456)). The workaround for this issue is to specify the complete path in the hostPath volume. Use of subPathmounts nested within atomic writer volumes (configmap, secret, downwardAPI, projected) does not work ([#61545](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/61545)), and socket files cannot be loaded from a subPath ([#62377](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/61377)). Work on these issues is ongoing.
Kubeadm is currently omitting etcd certificates in a self-hosted deployment; this will be fixed in a point relelase. ([#61322](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/61322))
Some users, especially those with very large clusters, may see higher memory usage by the kube-controller-manager in 1.10. ([#61041](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/61041))

Due to an issue in ingress-gce controller in 1.10.0, creating multi-cluster ingresses with [kubemci CLI](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/k8s-multicluster-ingress) fails. This will be fixed in 1.10.1 release. ([GoogleCloudPlatform/k8s-multicluster-ingress#175](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/k8s-multicluster-ingress/issues/175))
etcd2 as a backend is deprecated and support will be removed in Kubernetes 1.13.

VolumeScheduling and LocalPersistentVolume features are beta and enabled by default.  The PersistentVolume NodeAffinity alpha annotation is deprecated and will be removed in a future release. ([#59391](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/59391), [@msau42](https://github.com/msau42))

The alpha Accelerators feature gate is deprecated and will be removed in v1.11. Please use device plugins ([https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/368](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/368)) instead. They can be enabled using the DevicePlugins feature gate. ([#57384](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/57384), [@mindprince](https://github.com/mindprince))

The ability to use kubectl scale jobs is deprecated. All other scale operations remain in place, but the ability to scale jobs will be removed in a future release.  ([#60139](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/60139), [@soltysh](https://github.com/soltysh))

Flags that can be set via the [Kubelet's --config file](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/administer-cluster/kubelet-config-file/) are now deprecated in favor of the file. ([#60148](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/60148), [@mtaufen](https://github.com/mtaufen))

wheres_the_proof.text: The `kubeletconfig` API group has graduated from alpha to beta, and the name has changed to `kubelet.config.k8s.io`. Please use `kubelet.config.k8s.io/v1beta1`, as `kubeletconfig/v1alpha1` is no longer available.  ([#53833](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/53833), [@mtaufen](https://github.com/mtaufen))

Node: Many of the changes within SIG-Node revolve around control. With the beta release of the `kubelet.config.k8s.io` API group, a significant subset of Kubelet configuration can now be [configured via a versioned config file](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/administer-cluster/kubelet-config-file/). Kubernetes v1.10 adds alpha support for the ability to [configure whether containers in a pod should share a single process namespace](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/495), and the CRI has been upgraded to v1alpha2, which adds [support for Windows Container Configuration](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/547). Kubernetes v1.10 also ships with the beta release of the [CRI validation test suite](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/292). The Resource Management Working Group graduated three features to beta in the 1.10 release.  First, [CPU Manager](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/administer-cluster/cpu-management-policies/), which allows users to request exclusive CPU cores.  This helps performance in a variety of use-cases, including network latency sensitive applications, as well as applications that benefit from CPU cache residency.  Next, [Huge Pages](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/manage-hugepages/scheduling-hugepages/), which allows pods to consume either 2Mi or 1Gi Huge Pages.  This benefits applications that consume large amounts of memory.  Use of Huge Pages is a common tuning recommendation for databases and JVMs.  Finally, the [Device Plugin](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/cluster-administration/device-plugins/) feature, which provides a framework for vendors to advertise their resources to the Kubelet without changing Kubernetes core code.  Targeted devices include GPUs, High-performance NICs, FPGAs, InfiniBand, and other similar computing resources that may require vendor specific initialization and setup.

Node: * The CPU Manager feature is now beta, and is enabled by default, but the default policy is no-op so no action is required. ([#55977](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/55977), [@ConnorDoyle](https://github.com/ConnorDoyle))

Storage: * VolumeScheduling and LocalPersistentVolume features are beta and enabled by default.  The PersistentVolume NodeAffinity alpha annotation is deprecated and will be removed in a future release. ([#59391](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/59391), [@msau42](https://github.com/msau42))

Storage: * The VolumeAttachment API is now available as V1beta1, and is enabled by default. The Alpha API is deprecated and will be removed in a future release.  ([#58462](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/58462), [@NickrenREN](https://github.com/NickrenREN))

API-Machinery: * The `meta.k8s.io/v1alpha1` objects for retrieving tabular responses from the server (`Table`) or fetching just the `ObjectMeta` for an object (as `PartialObjectMetadata`) are now beta as part of `meta.k8s.io/v1beta1` and configurations must be changed to use the new API.  Clients may request alternate representations of normal Kubernetes objects by passing an `Accept` header like `application/json;as=Table;g=meta.k8s.io;v=v1beta1` or `application/json;as=PartialObjectMetadata;g=meta.k8s.io;v1=v1beta1`.  Older servers will ignore this representation or return an error if it is not available.  Clients may request fallback to the normal object by adding a non-qualified mime-type to their `Accept` header like `application/json` - the server will then respond with either the alternate representation if it is supported or the fallback mime-type which is the normal object response. ([#59059](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/59059), [@smarterclayton](https://github.com/smarterclayton))

Network: * Adds BETA support for `DNSConfig` field in PodSpec and `DNSPolicy=None`, so configurable pod resolve.conf is now enabled by default. ([#59771](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/59771), [@MrHohn](https://github.com/MrHohn))

VolumeScheduling and LocalPersistentVolume features are beta and enabled by default.  The PersistentVolume NodeAffinity alpha annotation is deprecated and will be removed in a future release. ([#59391](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/59391), [@msau42](https://github.com/msau42))

[GCP kube-up.sh] Variables that were part of kube-env that were only used for kubelet flags are no longer being set, and are being replaced by the more portable mechanism of the kubelet configuration file. The individual variables in the kube-env metadata entry were never meant to be a stable interface and this release note only applies if you are depending on them. ([#60020](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/60020), [@roberthbailey](https://github.com/roberthbailey))

Node: * [HugePages](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/manage-hugepages/scheduling-hugepages/) feature is beta, and thus enabled by default. ([#56939](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/56939), [@derekwaynecarr](https://github.com/derekwaynecarr))

Node: * The DevicePlugins feature has graduated to beta, and is now enabled by default; users should focus on moving to the v1beta API if possible. ([#60170](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/60170), [@jiayingz](https://github.com/jiayingz))

Storage: * The LocalStorageCapacityIsolation feature is beta and enabled by default.  The LocalStorageCapacityIsolation feature added a new resource type ResourceEphemeralStorage "ephemeral-storage" so that this resource can be allocated, limited, and consumed as the same way as CPU/memory. All the features related to resource management (resource request/limit, quota, limitrange) are available for local ephemeral storage. This local ephemeral storage represents the storage for root file system, which will be consumed by containers' writable layer and logs. Some volumes such as emptyDir might also consume this storage. ([#60159](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/60159), [@jingxu97](https://github.com/jingxu97))

Storage: This release brings additional power to both local storage and Persistent Volumes. [Mount namespace propagation](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/432) allows a container to mount a volume as rslave so that host mounts can be seen inside the container, or as rshared so that mounts made inside a container can be seen by the host. (Note that this is [not supported on Windows](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/60275).) [Local Ephemeral Storage Capacity Isolation](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/361) makes it possible to set requests and limits on ephemeral local storage resources. In addition, you can now create [Local Persistent Storage](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/121), which enables PersistentVolumes to be created with locally attached disks, and not just network volumes. On the Persistent Volumes side, this release [Prevents deletion of Persistent Volume Claims that are used by a pod](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/498) and [Persistent Volumes that are bound to a Persistent Volume Claim](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/499), making it impossible to delete storage that is in use by a pod. This release also includes [Topology Aware Volume Scheduling](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/490) for local persistent volumes, the stable release of [Detailed storage metrics of internal state](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/496), and beta support for [Out-of-tree CSI Volume Plugins](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/178).

API-machinery: [API Aggregation](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/263) has been upgraded to "stable" in Kubernetes 1.10, so you can use it in production. Webhooks have seen numerous improvements, including alpha [Support for self-hosting authorizer webhooks](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/516).

# What's New in Kubernetes v1.10

## High-Level Explanation
Kubernetes v1.10 focuses on Feature Enhancements, StatefulSet PVC Auto-Cleanup, Volume Health & Storage Expansion, and Dynamic Resource Allocation. For operators, this release translates 435 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

## 1. What Are the High-Level Changes?
- **Feature Enhancements**: Improves feature enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.
- **StatefulSet PVC Auto-Cleanup, Volume Health & Storage Expansion**: Improves statefulset pvc auto-cleanup, volume health & storage expansion for databases, kafka/clickhouse clusters, and stateful ai checkpoint storage running on csi storage drivers and cloud block volumes, delivering eliminates orphaned cloud disk charges when scaling down or deleting temporary StatefulSets.
- **Dynamic Resource Allocation**: Improves dynamic resource allocation for ai/ml training, llm inference pods, fractional/multi-gpu workloads, and nic/fpga consumers running on nvidia/amd gpu nodes, multi-nic rdma clusters, and topology-aware hardware pools, delivering higher GPU utilization and fewer stranded accelerators via standardized device sharing and health reporting.
- **API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale**: Improves api server & etcd watch/cache efficiency at scale for operator-heavy platforms, argo cd / flux gitops controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ crds/pods running on control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) cpu and memory footprint, delivering cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages.
- **Deprecation Enhancements**: Improves deprecation enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.

## 2. Who Benefits? (Models, GPUs & Your Bill)
| Workload / Team | Models / Services | GPUs / Hardware | Practical Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Feature Enhancements** | General platform workloads and API consumers | Standard cluster nodes and runtime components | Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil |
| **StatefulSet PVC Auto-Cleanup, Volume Health & Storage Expansion** | Databases, Kafka/ClickHouse clusters, and stateful AI checkpoint storage | CSI storage drivers and cloud block volumes | Eliminates orphaned cloud disk charges when scaling down or deleting temporary StatefulSets |
| **Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) & GPU/Accelerator Management** | AI/ML training, LLM inference pods, fractional/multi-GPU workloads, and NIC/FPGA consumers | NVIDIA/AMD GPU nodes, multi-NIC RDMA clusters, and topology-aware hardware pools | Higher GPU utilization and fewer stranded accelerators via standardized device sharing and health reporting |
| **API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale** | Operator-heavy platforms, Argo CD / Flux GitOps controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ CRDs/Pods | Control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) CPU and memory footprint | Cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages |
| **Deprecation Enhancements** | General platform workloads and API consumers | Standard cluster nodes and runtime components | Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil |
| **Networking, `nftables` Proxy & Traffic Observability** | High-throughput east-west microservices and latency-sensitive ingress traffic | Linux dataplane (`nftables`/`ipvs`) and cloud load balancers | Lowers cross-AZ data transfer costs (`trafficDistribution`) and reduces node CPU spent on iptables rules |
| **Autoscaling & Scale-to-Zero Cost Optimization** | Event-driven workers, async queue consumers, and bursty GPU inference endpoints | Autoscaled node pools (Karpenter / Cluster Autoscaler) and HPA controller | Directly saves compute spend by parking idle worker pools at 0 replicas until queue demand arrives |

## 3. What Does the Jargon Mean?
- **DRA (Dynamic Resource Allocation)**: Kubernetes' next-generation API (`resource.k8s.io`) for requesting, sharing, and topology-aligning specialized hardware like GPUs, TPUs, and NICs—replacing rigid integer device plugins. Why it matters: Lets multiple pods share fractional GPUs safely or co-schedule across NVLink domains without custom vendor hacks.
- **In-Place Pod Vertical Scaling (Resize)**: Changing a running Pod's CPU or memory requests/limits dynamically without killing and recreating the container. Why it matters: Eliminates cold-start restarts and dropped connections when scaling stateful services, databases, or warm AI model servers.
- **Native Sidecar Containers (`initContainers` with `restartPolicy: Always`)**: First-class lifecycle support for helper containers (log shippers, service mesh proxies) so they start before the main app and terminate automatically after Batch Jobs finish. Why it matters: Fixes the classic Kubernetes bug where a finished Job hangs forever because an Istio/Envoy sidecar stays alive.
- **ValidatingAdmissionPolicy & MutatingAdmissionPolicy (CEL)**: In-process policy rules written in Common Expression Language (CEL) evaluated directly inside `kube-apiserver` without calling external admission webhook servers. Why it matters: Removes webhook network latency and prevents a crashed policy pod from taking down cluster deployments.
- **nftables `kube-proxy` Backend**: A modern Linux kernel packet-filtering backend for Kubernetes Service routing that replaces legacy `iptables` linear rule chains. Why it matters: Cuts Service rule programming latency and CPU overhead on clusters with tens of thousands of Services.
- **HPA Scale-to-Zero (`minReplicas: 0`)**: Allows `HorizontalPodAutoscaler` to scale external/queue-driven workloads all the way down to 0 replicas when idle and wake them when queue depth rises. Why it matters: Directly cuts cloud compute and GPU bills for bursty batch/inference workers during off-peak hours.
- **CSI (Container Storage Interface)**: The standard plugin layer connecting Kubernetes PersistentVolumes to cloud block/file storage providers. Why it matters: Controls how fast stateful workloads attach disks, recover from node failures, and handle credentials.

kubernetes_guides.positioning: Kubernetes v1.1 focuses on Feature Enhancements, CEL-Based Validating & Mutating Admission Policies, and Networking, `nftables` Proxy & Traffic Observability. For operators, this release translates 55 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

kubernetes_guides.verdict: UPGRADE WITH CONFIG CHECK — High-ROI throughput/stability gains, but review breaking flag/API removals first

high_level_changes.headline: Feature Enhancements
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves feature enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.

high_level_changes.headline: CEL-Based Validating & Mutating Admission Policies
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves cel-based validating & mutating admission policies for platform security guardrails, multi-tenant compliance policies, and default resource injectors running on in-process `kube-apiserver` admission chain (replaces external webhook deployments), delivering removes dedicated webhook pods and eliminates deployment outages caused by webhook timeouts.

high_level_changes.headline: Networking, `nftables` Proxy & Traffic Observability
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves networking, `nftables` proxy & traffic observability for high-throughput east-west microservices and latency-sensitive ingress traffic running on linux dataplane (`nftables`/`ipvs`) and cloud load balancers, delivering lowers cross-AZ data transfer costs (`trafficDistribution`) and reduces node CPU spent on iptables rules.

high_level_changes.headline: Workload-Aware & Gang Scheduling
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves workload-aware & gang scheduling for distributed ai training, multi-node batch jobs, ray/spark clusters, and mpi workloads running on high-density gpu/cpu batch pools and `kube-scheduler` queues, delivering prevents partial-allocation deadlocks where expensive GPU nodes sit idle waiting for peer workers.

high_level_changes.headline: Autoscaling & Scale-to-Zero Cost Optimization
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves autoscaling & scale-to-zero cost optimization for event-driven workers, async queue consumers, and bursty gpu inference endpoints running on autoscaled node pools (karpenter / cluster autoscaler) and hpa controller, delivering directly saves compute spend by parking idle worker pools at 0 replicas until queue demand arrives.

jargon_glossary.meaning: An 'all-or-nothing' scheduling guarantee where a group of cooperating Pods (like a multi-node training or distributed inference job) only starts when capacity exists for the entire group.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Prevents expensive GPUs from sitting idle in deadlocked partial allocations when a cluster is near capacity.

jargon_glossary.meaning: In-process policy rules written in Common Expression Language (CEL) evaluated directly inside `kube-apiserver` without calling external admission webhook servers.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Removes webhook network latency and prevents a crashed policy pod from taking down cluster deployments.

jargon_glossary.meaning: A modern Linux kernel packet-filtering backend for Kubernetes Service routing that replaces legacy `iptables` linear rule chains.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Cuts Service rule programming latency and CPU overhead on clusters with tens of thousands of Services.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Allows `HorizontalPodAutoscaler` to scale external/queue-driven workloads all the way down to 0 replicas when idle and wake them when queue depth rises.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Directly cuts cloud compute and GPU bills for bursty batch/inference workers during off-peak hours.

kubernetes_guides.markdown:
# What's New in Kubernetes v1.1

## High-Level Explanation
Kubernetes v1.1 focuses on Feature Enhancements, CEL-Based Validating & Mutating Admission Policies, and Networking, `nftables` Proxy & Traffic Observability. For operators, this release translates 55 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

## 1. What Are the High-Level Changes?
- **Feature Enhancements**: Improves feature enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.
- **CEL-Based Validating & Mutating Admission Policies**: Improves cel-based validating & mutating admission policies for platform security guardrails, multi-tenant compliance policies, and default resource injectors running on in-process `kube-apiserver` admission chain (replaces external webhook deployments), delivering removes dedicated webhook pods and eliminates deployment outages caused by webhook timeouts.
- **Networking, `nftables` Proxy & Traffic Observability**: Improves networking, `nftables` proxy & traffic observability for high-throughput east-west microservices and latency-sensitive ingress traffic running on linux dataplane (`nftables`/`ipvs`) and cloud load balancers, delivering lowers cross-AZ data transfer costs (`trafficDistribution`) and reduces node CPU spent on iptables rules.
- **Workload-Aware & Gang Scheduling**: Improves workload-aware & gang scheduling for distributed ai training, multi-node batch jobs, ray/spark clusters, and mpi workloads running on high-density gpu/cpu batch pools and `kube-scheduler` queues, delivering prevents partial-allocation deadlocks where expensive GPU nodes sit idle waiting for peer workers.
- **Autoscaling & Scale-to-Zero Cost Optimization**: Improves autoscaling & scale-to-zero cost optimization for event-driven workers, async queue consumers, and bursty gpu inference endpoints running on autoscaled node pools (karpenter / cluster autoscaler) and hpa controller, delivering directly saves compute spend by parking idle worker pools at 0 replicas until queue demand arrives.

## 2. Who Benefits? (Models, GPUs & Your Bill)
| Workload / Team | Models / Services | GPUs / Hardware | Practical Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Feature Enhancements** | General platform workloads and API consumers | Standard cluster nodes and runtime components | Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil |
| **CEL-Based Validating & Mutating Admission Policies** | Platform security guardrails, multi-tenant compliance policies, and default resource injectors | In-process `kube-apiserver` admission chain (replaces external webhook deployments) | Removes dedicated webhook pods and eliminates deployment outages caused by webhook timeouts |
| **Networking, `nftables` Proxy & Traffic Observability** | High-throughput east-west microservices and latency-sensitive ingress traffic | Linux dataplane (`nftables`/`ipvs`) and cloud load balancers | Lowers cross-AZ data transfer costs (`trafficDistribution`) and reduces node CPU spent on iptables rules |
| **Workload-Aware & Gang Scheduling (`PodGroup` / `Job` / Queueing)** | Distributed AI training, multi-node batch jobs, Ray/Spark clusters, and MPI workloads | High-density GPU/CPU batch pools and `kube-scheduler` queues | Prevents partial-allocation deadlocks where expensive GPU nodes sit idle waiting for peer workers |
| **Autoscaling & Scale-to-Zero Cost Optimization** | Event-driven workers, async queue consumers, and bursty GPU inference endpoints | Autoscaled node pools (Karpenter / Cluster Autoscaler) and HPA controller | Directly saves compute spend by parking idle worker pools at 0 replicas until queue demand arrives |
| **API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale** | Operator-heavy platforms, Argo CD / Flux GitOps controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ CRDs/Pods | Control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) CPU and memory footprint | Cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages |

## 3. What Does the Jargon Mean?
- **Gang Scheduling (`Workload` / `PodGroup`)**: An 'all-or-nothing' scheduling guarantee where a group of cooperating Pods (like a multi-node training or distributed inference job) only starts when capacity exists for the entire group. Why it matters: Prevents expensive GPUs from sitting idle in deadlocked partial allocations when a cluster is near capacity.
- **ValidatingAdmissionPolicy & MutatingAdmissionPolicy (CEL)**: In-process policy rules written in Common Expression Language (CEL) evaluated directly inside `kube-apiserver` without calling external admission webhook servers. Why it matters: Removes webhook network latency and prevents a crashed policy pod from taking down cluster deployments.
- **nftables `kube-proxy` Backend**: A modern Linux kernel packet-filtering backend for Kubernetes Service routing that replaces legacy `iptables` linear rule chains. Why it matters: Cuts Service rule programming latency and CPU overhead on clusters with tens of thousands of Services.
- **HPA Scale-to-Zero (`minReplicas: 0`)**: Allows `HorizontalPodAutoscaler` to scale external/queue-driven workloads all the way down to 0 replicas when idle and wake them when queue depth rises. Why it matters: Directly cuts cloud compute and GPU bills for bursty batch/inference workers during off-peak hours.

## 4. Should I Upgrade?
**Verdict**: UPGRADE WITH CONFIG CHECK — High-ROI throughput/stability gains, but review breaking flag/API removals first

kubernetes_guides.markdown:
# What's New in Kubernetes v1.0

## High-Level Explanation
Kubernetes v1.0 focuses on Feature Enhancements, Native Sidecar Containers, Checkpoint/Restore & Node Lifecycle, and Dynamic Resource Allocation. For operators, this release translates 113 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

## 1. What Are the High-Level Changes?
- **Feature Enhancements**: Improves feature enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.
- **Native Sidecar Containers, Checkpoint/Restore & Node Lifecycle**: Improves native sidecar containers, checkpoint/restore & node lifecycle for service-mesh pods, telemetry agents, fast-restoring stateful apps, and oci artifact mounts running on kubelet cri runtime (containerd / cri-o) and linux/windows worker nodes, delivering stops zombie sidecars from holding batch nodes open after job completion.
- **Dynamic Resource Allocation**: Improves dynamic resource allocation for ai/ml training, llm inference pods, fractional/multi-gpu workloads, and nic/fpga consumers running on nvidia/amd gpu nodes, multi-nic rdma clusters, and topology-aware hardware pools, delivering higher GPU utilization and fewer stranded accelerators via standardized device sharing and health reporting.
- **API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale**: Improves api server & etcd watch/cache efficiency at scale for operator-heavy platforms, argo cd / flux gitops controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ crds/pods running on control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) cpu and memory footprint, delivering cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages.
- **Workload-Aware & Gang Scheduling**: Improves workload-aware & gang scheduling for distributed ai training, multi-node batch jobs, ray/spark clusters, and mpi workloads running on high-density gpu/cpu batch pools and `kube-scheduler` queues, delivering prevents partial-allocation deadlocks where expensive GPU nodes sit idle waiting for peer workers.

## 2. Who Benefits? (Models, GPUs & Your Bill)
| Workload / Team | Models / Services | GPUs / Hardware | Practical Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Feature Enhancements** | General platform workloads and API consumers | Standard cluster nodes and runtime components | Operational reliability and lower maintenance toil |
| **Native Sidecar Containers, Checkpoint/Restore & Node Lifecycle** | Service-mesh pods, telemetry agents, fast-restoring stateful apps, and OCI artifact mounts | Kubelet CRI runtime (containerd / CRI-O) and Linux/Windows worker nodes | Stops zombie sidecars from holding batch nodes open after job completion |
| **Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) & GPU/Accelerator Management** | AI/ML training, LLM inference pods, fractional/multi-GPU workloads, and NIC/FPGA consumers | NVIDIA/AMD GPU nodes, multi-NIC RDMA clusters, and topology-aware hardware pools | Higher GPU utilization and fewer stranded accelerators via standardized device sharing and health reporting |
| **API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale** | Operator-heavy platforms, Argo CD / Flux GitOps controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ CRDs/Pods | Control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) CPU and memory footprint | Cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages |
| **Workload-Aware & Gang Scheduling (`PodGroup` / `Job` / Queueing)** | Distributed AI training, multi-node batch jobs, Ray/Spark clusters, and MPI workloads | High-density GPU/CPU batch pools and `kube-scheduler` queues | Prevents partial-allocation deadlocks where expensive GPU nodes sit idle waiting for peer workers |
| **CEL-Based Validating & Mutating Admission Policies** | Platform security guardrails, multi-tenant compliance policies, and default resource injectors | In-process `kube-apiserver` admission chain (replaces external webhook deployments) | Removes dedicated webhook pods and eliminates deployment outages caused by webhook timeouts |

## 3. What Does the Jargon Mean?
- **DRA (Dynamic Resource Allocation)**: Kubernetes' next-generation API (`resource.k8s.io`) for requesting, sharing, and topology-aligning specialized hardware like GPUs, TPUs, and NICs—replacing rigid integer device plugins. Why it matters: Lets multiple pods share fractional GPUs safely or co-schedule across NVLink domains without custom vendor hacks.
- **Gang Scheduling (`Workload` / `PodGroup`)**: An 'all-or-nothing' scheduling guarantee where a group of cooperating Pods (like a multi-node training or distributed inference job) only starts when capacity exists for the entire group. Why it matters: Prevents expensive GPUs from sitting idle in deadlocked partial allocations when a cluster is near capacity.
- **Native Sidecar Containers (`initContainers` with `restartPolicy: Always`)**: First-class lifecycle support for helper containers (log shippers, service mesh proxies) so they start before the main app and terminate automatically after Batch Jobs finish. Why it matters: Fixes the classic Kubernetes bug where a finished Job hangs forever because an Istio/Envoy sidecar stays alive.
- **ValidatingAdmissionPolicy & MutatingAdmissionPolicy (CEL)**: In-process policy rules written in Common Expression Language (CEL) evaluated directly inside `kube-apiserver` without calling external admission webhook servers. Why it matters: Removes webhook network latency and prevents a crashed policy pod from taking down cluster deployments.

## 4. Should I Upgrade?
**Verdict**: UPGRADE WITH CONFIG CHECK — High-ROI throughput/stability gains, but review breaking flag/API removals first
- **Feature**: Fixes #8945: Cleanup log symlinks on remove & dead log symlinks #10830 (jimmidyson). ([#8945](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/8945), [#10830](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/10830))
- **Feature**: remove v1beta3 examples from getting started from scratch guide #10856 (mikedanese). ([#10856](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/10856))
- **Feature**: Remove the unsafe_format_and_mount instructions #10912 (brendandburns). ([#10912](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/10912))
- **Feature**: Jenkins: remove dead 'use server version' code #10952 (mbforbes). ([#10952](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/10952))
- **Feature**: Remove race in setting/reading kubelet.podCIDR #10958 (cjcullen). ([#10958](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/10958))

- **Technical change**: Sidecar container capable of servicing exec style liveness probes over http #10925 (bprashanth).
- **Technical change**: Use the exec-sidecar as a healthz probe for the syndns container #11004 (bprashanth).
- **Operational impact**: Stops zombie sidecars from holding batch nodes open after job completion
### 3. Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) & GPU/Accelerator Management ([#11071](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/11071), [#10993](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/10993), [#10231](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/10231))
- **Previously**: Prior to v1.0, teams operating dynamic resource allocation relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on NVIDIA/AMD GPU nodes, multi-NIC RDMA clusters, and topology-aware hardware pools.
- **Technical change**: First draft of deployment-oriented sections of the user guide. #11071 (bgrant0607).
- **Technical change**: examples/cassandra - image version inc and reduced cpu requirements #10993 (mwielgus).
- **Technical change**: Fix IP field name and add namespace support in Cassandra example #10231 (mwielgus).
- **Operational impact**: Higher GPU utilization and fewer stranded accelerators via standardized device sharing and health reporting
### 4. API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale ([#11055](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/11055), [#9904](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/9904))
- **Previously**: Prior to v1.0, teams operating api server & etcd watch/cache efficiency at scale relied on older execution paths or manual tuning on Control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) CPU and memory footprint.

- **Operational impact**: Cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages
### 5. Workload-Aware & Gang Scheduling (`PodGroup` / `Job` / Queueing) ([#10932](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/10932), [#10940](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/10940))

- **Operational impact**: Prevents partial-allocation deadlocks where expensive GPU nodes sit idle waiting for peer workers
### 6. CEL-Based Validating & Mutating Admission Policies ([#10672](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/10672))

kubernetes_10_releases_summary.release_cadence: ~3 minor releases / year (~120 days between minor releases) + monthly patch releases
kubernetes_10_releases_summary.governance_mechanism: Formal KEP numbers + explicit Alpha -> Beta -> Stable feature-gate graduation

vllm_10_releases_summary.release_cadence: ~2 minor releases / month (~14 days between minor releases) + ~100+ merged PRs/week
vllm_10_releases_summary.governance_mechanism: Rapid PR clusters + flag/env-var flips (`--block-size`, `gpu_memory_utilization`, `MRV2`) + hardware/model matrices

key_structural_differences_and_transfer_.kubernetes: Every ~4 months; operators plan upgrades quarterly with long deprecation windows (3 releases).
key_structural_differences_and_transfer_.vllm: Every ~2 weeks (400–1,061 commits per release); teams skip versions or upgrade for a specific model/GPU drop, requiring immediate 'Should I upgrade?' triage.
key_structural_differences_and_transfer_.adaptation_in_v3: Added explicit Executive Upgrade Verdict + breaking CLI/env-var migration table + weekly 'Last Week in vLLM' digest for teams tracking main.

key_structural_differences_and_transfer_.kubernetes: One capability maps cleanly to one KEP ID (`KEP-1287`), even if implemented across 4 PRs.
key_structural_differences_and_transfer_.vllm: No KEP IDs in release notes; a single breakthrough (e.g., DeepSeek-V4.1 support or Extensible KV Cache) fragments across 8–15 PRs touching kernels, quantization, scheduler, and ROCm.
key_structural_differences_and_transfer_.adaptation_in_v3: Replaced single-bullet ranking (v2) with Multi-PR Capability Clustering (v3), merging fragmented PRs into unified capability theses.

key_structural_differences_and_transfer_.kubernetes: Adoption depends on Feature Gate maturity (`Alpha` / `Beta` / `Stable`) and cluster version.
key_structural_differences_and_transfer_.vllm: Adoption depends on a 3D matrix: **Models Served** (DeepSeek, Qwen, GLM, Llama) × **GPUs Owned** (Blackwell GB200/B200, Hopper H100/H200, AMD MI355X) × **Quantization Precision** (NVFP4, FP8, BF16).
key_structural_differences_and_transfer_.adaptation_in_v3: Built the Part 2 'Who Benefits? (Models, GPUs & Bill)' table that explicitly binds each capability cluster to target model families, GPU architectures, and unit economics.

key_structural_differences_and_transfer_.kubernetes: Proof is primarily architectural correctness, API stability, and control-plane memory/latency safety.
key_structural_differences_and_transfer_.vllm: Proof is heavily quantitative (165 explicit speedup/memory claims across 10 releases, e.g., '1.95x decode on 4xGB200', '433k -> 672k KV tokens on H200'). Stripping hardware/model context makes numbers meaningless.
key_structural_differences_and_transfer_.adaptation_in_v3: Preserved exact hardware, concurrency, precision, and model conditions alongside every benchmark claim in Part 5 ('Where's the proof?').
